summary: Gan and Ichino describe the automorphic discrete spectrum of the metaplectic group Mp_2n over a number field, generalizing Waldspurger's Shimura correspondence for Mp_2. Theorem 1.1 (unconditional): L²_disc(Mp_2n) decomposes into near equivalence classes L²_{φ,ψ}(Mp_2n) indexed by Arthur's elliptic A-parameters φ, which are also those of SO_2n+1. Theorem 1.4: for generic φ, L²_{φ,ψ}(Mp_2n) ≅ ⊕_η m_η π_η, with m_η = 1 exactly when Δ*η = ε_φ, the product of the root numbers ε(1/2, φ_i); here π_η is built from the local Langlands correspondence for Mp_2n defined through the local Shimura correspondence (theta lifts to SO(V⁺) ⊔ SO(V⁻)). Hence the generic part is multiplicity-free (Corollary 1.6). Theorem 1.4 assumes Arthur's multiplicity formula for non-split SO_2n+1, which Ishimoto proved for generic parameters in 2024. The method avoids the vanishing of central L-values by working in the stable range: J.-S. Li's lift to SO_2r+1 with r > 2n + 1 carries L²_disc(Mp_2n) into Arthur's classification (Theorem 2.1, Proposition 3.1). For generic φ every such form is cuspidal (Proposition 4.1), which gives multiplicity preservation (Corollary 4.2). The local structure is then identified with the local Shimura correspondence (Propositions 5.4 and 6.1), by irreducibility of induced representations and a global argument through globalizations with L(1/2, Φ) ≠ 0 (Appendix A). The atlas plans the metaplectic covers, the Weil representation, local theta modules and theta kernels (MetaplecticAutomorphicForms MP.1–MP.5), and Arthur's classification (ML.4). It has nothing for the theta correspondence as a correspondence: Howe duality and conservation, the local Shimura correspondence, J.-S. Li's stable-range theory, the Rallis inner product formula, or the discrete spectrum of Mp_2n. Of 89 items, one is in the libraries (the spinor norm, in Tau Ceti), 18 are planned and 70 are missing. The missing items go to a Part II of MetaplecticAutomorphicForms (57), with sources for MP.3 (5), ML.4 (4), ML.5 (2), AF.1 (1) and AL.3 (1). Four source issues: three proof steps asserted without proof (E1–E3), and a wrong reference [44] in the published version (E4). After the review (REV-PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18) there are 104 items (1 library, 21 planned, 82 missing) and 7 source issues. E1–E3 are rejected: each step is covered by the cited source. The review found that Proposition A.2 is unproved as printed for n ≥ 2, because the cited Jiang–Soudry Th. 2.2(2) fails there. Its hypothesis should require θ_{ψ_{v0}}(π_{v0}) to be supercuspidal, which is the case in the only application, so Theorems 1.1 and 1.4 stand. The proof of Proposition 3.1 also needs a one-line non-vanishing input.

items.name: The local metaplectic group Mp_2n and its genuine representations
items.statement: Let F be a local field of characteristic zero and n ≥ 0 (Sp_0 = {1}). Mp_2n is the two-fold topological central extension 1 → {±1} → Mp_2n → Sp_2n(F) → 1 which is the unique (up to unique isomorphism) nonsplit two-fold topological central extension of Sp_2n(F) when n > 0 and F ≠ C, and the trivial extension Sp_2n(F) × {±1} when n = 0 or F = C. It is realized on the set Sp_2n(F) × {±1} with multiplication given by Ranga Rao's 2-cocycle. A representation of Mp_2n is genuine if −1 ∈ {±1} acts by −1; Irr Mp_2n is the set of equivalence classes of irreducible genuine smooth representations.
items.note: MP.1 constructs the double cover from the normalized Weil-index cocycle (Ranga Rao's cocycle, Pacific J. Math. 157 (1993), is an explicit normalization of it) and exports genuine representations. The uniqueness assertion is Moore's theorem; the paper states it without proof and does not use it. Mathlib has the symplectic matrix group (Matrix.symplecticGroup, read at 082e2d3); neither library has the cover (library audit: MP.1 not built). Review note: Status planned is right. MetaplecticAutomorphicForms:MP.1 plans the double cover from the normalized Weil-index cocycle and exports genuine representations. mathlib:Matrix.symplecticGroup read at 082e2d3 (Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/SymplecticGroup.lean:101; a Submonoid of Matrix (l ⊕ l) (l ⊕ l) R, so the group of units is what the item needs). Moore's uniqueness is stated on p. 973 but never used.

items.name: The adelic metaplectic group and its genuine automorphic forms
items.statement: For a number field F with adèle ring A, Mp_2n(A) is the two-fold cover 1 → {±1} → Mp_2n(A) → Sp_2n(A) → 1, which splits canonically over Sp_2n(F); Sp_2n(F) is regarded as a subgroup of Mp_2n(A) through this splitting. L²(Mp_2n) is the subspace of L²(Sp_2n(F)\Mp_2n(A)) on which {±1} acts by the nontrivial character. A(Mp_2n) is the space of genuine automorphic forms on Mp_2n(A), and A²(Mp_2n) and A_cusp(Mp_2n) are its subspaces of square-integrable automorphic forms and of cusp forms.
items.locator: §1.1, p. 966; Notation, p. 973; §2.1, pp. 973–974 (the adelic cover is at the foot of p. 973, and 'This cover splits over Sp_2n(F) canonically' is on p. 974) (arXiv v3 pp. 2, 7)
items.note: MP.4 constructs the restricted product of the local covers, the canonical splitting over the rational points and the adelic Weil representation. MP.5 constructs genuine cusp and Eisenstein spaces on the cover, constant terms and Fourier–Whittaker expansions. Review note: MP.4 plans the restricted-product cover and the canonical rational splitting, and MP.5 plans the genuine cusp and Eisenstein spaces. Neither names L²(Mp_2n) or A²(Mp_2n) (square-integrable genuine forms); AS.4 plans those for linear groups only. So 'planned' holds for the group and cusp forms, and the L² part goes with item discrete-spectrum (route 1).

items.name: Odd-dimensional quadratic spaces, SO(V) and the Hasse–Witt invariant
items.statement: A quadratic space V over F is a finite-dimensional F-vector space with a nondegenerate quadratic form q. Here dim V = 2r + 1 and the discriminant of q is trivial. V is split if it is isometric to H^r ⊕ F, where H is the hyperbolic plane and F carries q(x) = x²; SO(V) is then written SO_2r+1 and is split. O(V) is the orthogonal group and SO(V) = O(V)⁰ its special orthogonal group, and O(V) = SO(V) × {±1} (2.1). For F local, ε(V) ∈ {±1} is the normalized Hasse–Witt invariant (Scharlau, pp. 80–81), with ε(V) = 1 if V is split. For F nonarchimedean and n ≥ 1 there are exactly two (2n + 1)-dimensional quadratic spaces with trivial discriminant up to isometry, V⁺ and V⁻, with SO(V⁺) split.
items.note: Tau Ceti has, at f790474: the orthogonal and special orthogonal groups of a quadratic map (orthogonalGroup, and specialOrthogonalGroup = orthogonalGroup ⊓ ker det); the hyperbolic plane ⟨1, −1⟩ over a ring with 2 invertible; and the signed discriminant of an isometry class of regular forms. The Hasse invariant and the classification over nonarchimedean local fields by (dimension, discriminant, Hasse invariant), with realization, are planned in Quadratic forms and cohomological invariants 6C–6D; real forms by signature in Global quadratic forms over number fields, Layer 1. The library audit (GN.2) records the Hasse–Witt invariant and the nonarchimedean classification as absent. 'Exactly two' is that classification in odd dimension. Review note: Library claims checked at f790474: TauCeti.QuadraticMap.orthogonalGroup (LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/OrthogonalGroup.lean:133); specialOrthogonalGroup = orthogonalGroup ⊓ ker det (same file, :290); TauCeti.hyperbolicPlane R = ⟨1, −1⟩ with [Invertible (2 : R)] (QuadraticForm/Hyperbolic.lean:68); TauCeti.RegularFormClass.signedDiscr (RegularFormClass/Discriminant.lean:157). The 6C stage plans localHasse q = ∏_{i<j} (a_i, a_j), which is NOT the paper's normalized ε: on the split space H^r ⊕ ⟨1⟩ it equals (−1,−1)^{r(r−1)/2}, which is −1 over Q_2 for r = 2 or 3. A normalization with ε(split) = 1 is ε(V) = localHasse(V)·localHasse(H^r ⊕ ⟨1⟩) (same dimension and discriminant). That one-line definition is planned nowhere and belongs in the Part II (route 1). 6D (classification and realization, dimension ≥ 3) gives 'exactly two' for n ≥ 1.

items.name: Global quadratic spaces with prescribed localizations
items.statement: Let F be a number field and n ≥ 0. For each place v let V_v be a (2n + 1)-dimensional quadratic space over F_v with trivial discriminant, split for almost all v, and let ε(V_v) ∈ {±1} be its normalized Hasse–Witt invariant (ε = 1 for split spaces). There is a (2n + 1)-dimensional quadratic space V over F with trivial discriminant and V ⊗ F_v ≅ V_v for all v if and only if ∏_v ε(V_v) = 1, and then V is unique up to isometry. In particular ∏_v ε(V ⊗ F_v) = 1 for every (2n + 1)-dimensional quadratic space V over F with trivial discriminant.
items.locator: Proofs of Lemmas 6.10–6.12, pp. 997–1000 (arXiv v3 pp. 26–28)
items.note: Used without statement: for the existence and uniqueness of V in Lemmas 6.10 and 6.12 and for the product formula that gives the contradiction in Lemma 6.11. Existence with prescribed local behaviour (O'Meara 72:1) is Global quadratic forms Layer 7.2; uniqueness is the classification of Layer 8.1. Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18): statement corrected against the paper: The last sentence claims '∏_v ε(V_v) = 1 for every quadratic space V over F'. But ε is the normalized Hasse–Witt invariant, which the paper defines (§2.1, p. 974) only for odd-dimensional spaces with trivial discriminant, normalized so that ε = 1 for split spaces. The product formula should therefore be stated for (2n + 1)-dimensional V with trivial discriminant. Review note: The status 'planned' is right. GlobalQuadraticForms Layer 7.2 plans O'Meara 72:1 (existence with prescribed forms at every finite, real and complex place), and Layer 8.1 plans the classification (uniqueness). The 'in particular' product formula is Layer 4.4 ('Also prove the Hasse-invariant product formula for one global form'), with 3.3, so add tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/GlobalQuadraticForms#layer-4-global-square-norm-and-approximation-lemmas to planned. The roadmap works with the plain Hasse sign. A short bridge to the paper's normalized invariant (Scharlau pp. 80–81) is needed: for fixed dimension and discriminant the two differ by a product of Hilbert symbols of fixed elements, whose product over all places is 1. In Lemma 6.12 a real V_v is fixed by ξ_v through the bijection (5.3), and ε(V_v) = ξ_v(z_{Φ_v}) by the inclusion Ŝ_{φ,V} ⊂ {η(z_φ) = ε(V)}. So ∏_v ε(V_v) = (⊗ξ_v)(Δ z_Φ) = 1 by (6.3). The paper leaves this step implicit, but it is correct.

items.name: The spinor norm
items.statement: ν : SO_2r+1 → F^×/(F^×)² is the spinor norm.
items.note: Tau Ceti (f790474): CliffordAlgebra.spinorNorm (Q : QuadraticForm K V) (hQ : Q.Nondegenerate) : specialOrthogonalGroup Q →* Multiplicative (SquareClassGroup K), for a field K with 2 invertible and V finite-dimensional; it restricts orthogonalSpinorNorm, the Clifford norm modulo squares. Review note: Library status confirmed at f790474: CliffordAlgebra.spinorNorm (Q : QuadraticForm K V) (hQ : Q.Nondegenerate) : QuadraticMap.specialOrthogonalGroup Q →* Multiplicative (SquareClassGroup K) (LinearAlgebra/CliffordAlgebra/Spin/SpinorNorm/Basic.lean:213), the restriction of orthogonalSpinorNorm. The Q(v) versus 2Q(v) convention for reflections does not matter on SO, where elements are products of an even number of reflections.

items.name: The local Langlands correspondence for GL_n over p-adic fields
items.statement: Let F be a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero and L_F = W_F × SL_2(C) its Weil–Deligne group. There is a bijection τ ↔ φ between Irr GL_n(F) and the set of equivalence classes of n-dimensional representations φ of L_F that are continuous and semisimple on W_F and algebraic on SL_2(C) (equivalently, n-dimensional Frobenius-semisimple Weil–Deligne representations) (Harris–Taylor; Henniart; Scholze). If τ ↔ φ, then τ is essentially square-integrable if and only if φ is irreducible, and τ is tempered if and only if φ is tempered, i.e. φ(W_F) is relatively compact in GL_n(C).
items.note: ET.6 constructs the characteristic-zero correspondence with full Weil–Deligne parameters, following Scholze, with the segment and Langlands-quotient theory. Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18): statement corrected against the paper: 'n-dimensional representations of L_F' leaves out the admissibility condition. The bijection is with Frobenius-semisimple Weil–Deligne representations, i.e. representations of W_F × SL_2(C) that are continuous and semisimple on W_F and algebraic on SL_2(C). Without that condition the set on the right is larger than Irr GL_n(F). The paper is just as terse (p. 985), but the item should be exact. Review note: ET.6 (read in data/atlas.json) constructs the characteristic-zero p-adic correspondence with full Frobenius-semisimple Weil–Deligne parameters. It also develops the segment/Langlands-quotient theory, including σ ⊗ Sp_r for essentially square-integrable segments, and the classification and induction compatibilities. So 'planned' is correct.

items.name: The local Langlands correspondence for GL_n(R) and GL_n(C)
items.statement: For F = R or C, with L_F the Weil group of F, Langlands' classification gives a bijection Irr GL_n(F) ↔ {n-dimensional semisimple representations of L_F}, under which τ is essentially square-integrable if and only if φ is irreducible and tempered if and only if φ is tempered. Every irreducible representation of L_C = C^× is 1-dimensional, and every irreducible symplectic representation of L_R is 2-dimensional.
items.locator: §1.1 (p. 967), §5.1 (p. 985), §6.1 (p. 992: 'any irreducible representation of L_C is 1-dimensional') and §6.2 (pp. 994–995: 'any irreducible symplectic representation of L_R is 2-dimensional'; 'any irreducible representation of L_C is 1-dimensional'), pp. 967–995 (arXiv v3 pp. 2–24)
items.note: Langlands, 'On the classification of irreducible representations of real algebraic groups' (Math. Surveys Monogr. 31). Routed to AF.1 as in PAPER-CHENEVIER-TAIBI-20 (item archimedean-llc-gln): no layer plans the archimedean correspondence. Review note: The locator's range stops at p. 993 and misses both places where the paper states the two dimension facts (pp. 992 and 994–995). 'Missing' is correct. AF.1 (read) builds (g,K)-modules, infinitesimal characters, Casselman–Wallach globalizations and relative Lie algebra cohomology, but not the Langlands classification or Weil-group parameters, and no other stage plans the archimedean correspondence (an atlas search for Langlands classification or W_R finds nothing). Route 5 therefore adds new content to AF.1, following the precedent of PAPER-CHENEVIER-TAIBI-20.

items.name: Symplectic and orthogonal self-dual cuspidal representations
items.statement: Let φ_i be an irreducible self-dual cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_{n_i}(A). The Rankin–Selberg L-function L(s, φ_i × φ_i^∨) = L(s, φ_i × φ_i) = L(s, φ_i, ∧²) L(s, φ_i, Sym²) has a simple pole at s = 1 (Jacquet–Shalika, Amer. J. Math. 103, Prop. 3.6), and neither factor vanishes at s = 1 (Shahidi, Amer. J. Math. 103, Th. 5.1). Hence exactly one of L(s, φ_i, ∧²) and L(s, φ_i, Sym²) has a pole at s = 1: φ_i is symplectic in the first case and orthogonal in the second. If φ_i is symplectic then n_i is even (Jacquet–Shalika, 'Exterior square L-functions', §9).
items.locator: §1.1 and proof of Lemma 4.3, pp. 967–982 (arXiv v3 pp. 2–14)
items.note: Planned in ML.4 as in PAPER-CHENEVIER-TAIBI-20 (item arthur-selfdual-types): Arthur's classification rests on this dichotomy. The analytic theory of the exterior and symmetric square L-functions (Bump–Friedberg, Jacquet–Shalika, Shahidi, Bump–Ginzburg) is cited; AL.3 plans the Rankin–Selberg pole. Partial L-functions are meant throughout. Review note: 'Planned in ML.4' is only partly supported. ML.4 (read) plans the Arthur/Mok/KMSW classification inputs: 'stabilization, transfer, fundamental lemma, packets, multiplicities and local-global compatibilities'. AL.3 plans the Rankin–Selberg pole of L(s, φ_i × φ_i^∨). No stage plans the exterior- and symmetric-square L-functions (Bump–Friedberg, Jacquet–Shalika, Bump–Ginzburg, Shahidi) or Shahidi's nonvanishing at s = 1 (Amer. J. Math. 103, Th. 5.1). Atlas searches for exterior square, symmetric square and Shahidi return no automorphic stage. Recommend status 'missing', routed as a source to ML.4 (route 3). Alternatively keep 'planned', but ML.4's blueprint must then name these analytic inputs. Citation detail: the paper's [37] is Jacquet–Shalika II, Amer. J. Math. 103 (1981), 777–815, and 'Amer. J. Math. 103' alone does not distinguish it from part I.

items.name: Strong multiplicity one for isobaric representations
items.statement: For cuspidal automorphic representations σ_1, …, σ_r of GL_{n_1}(A), …, GL_{n_r}(A) (not necessarily unitary), the isobaric sum σ_1 ⊞ ⋯ ⊞ σ_r is the irreducible automorphic representation of GL_N(A), N = Σ_i n_i, whose local component at every place v is the Langlands quotient of the representation parabolically induced from σ_{1,v} ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ σ_{r,v}; equivalently, via the local Langlands correspondence, its L-parameter at v is the direct sum of those of the σ_{i,v}. Strong multiplicity one (Jacquet–Shalika, 'On Euler products and the classification of automorphic forms II', Amer. J. Math. 103 (1981), 777–815, Th. 4.4): if σ_1 ⊞ ⋯ ⊞ σ_r and σ′_1 ⊞ ⋯ ⊞ σ′_{r′} have isomorphic local components at almost all places, then r = r′ and, after renumbering, σ′_i ≅ σ_i for every i.
items.locator: Proofs of Propositions 3.1 and 4.1, pp. 978–980 (arXiv v3 pp. 11–12)
items.note: Used to show the A-parameter of Proposition 3.1 is unique, and to compare the two weak lifts (4.1) and (4.2) in Proposition 4.1. AL.3 plans Rankin–Selberg theory with its poles; this consequence is not planned anywhere (R16.4 plans only the GL_2 case). Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18): statement corrected against the paper: The item relies on 'isobaric sums' without defining them. Propositions 3.1 and 4.1 need that definition, and so does the proposed weak-lift item. The citation 'Amer. J. Math. 103 (1981)' covers both Jacquet–Shalika papers; the theorem is in part II ([37], pp. 777–815). Review note: 'Missing' is confirmed. AL.3 (read) plans the Rankin–Selberg integrals with their poles, from which JS II Th. 4.4 follows. R16.4 plans strong multiplicity one only for GL_2. No stage plans the isobaric version. Route 6 fits.

items.name: The partial standard L-function of a genuine representation relative to ψ
items.statement: Let π = ⊗_v π_v be an irreducible genuine representation of Mp_2n(A), unramified outside a finite set S of places containing the archimedean and dyadic places and those where ψ_v is not of order zero. L^S_ψ(s, π) = ∏_{v∉S} L(s, ϕ_v), where ϕ_v : L_{F_v} → Sp_2n(C) is the L-parameter of π_v relative to ψ_v (Remark 5.3) composed with the standard representation of Sp_2n(C). For π occurring in L²_disc(Mp_2n), L^S_ψ(s, π) is holomorphic for Re s > n + 1 (Yamana, Invent. Math. 196, Th. 9.1).
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 3.1, (3.3); proof of Lemma 6.8, pp. 977–997 (arXiv v3 pp. 10–25)
items.note: AL.4 builds partial Euler products from Satake classes, with convergence where an eigenvalue bound is supplied. The ψ-relative parameter is item rmk-5-3. Review note: 'Planned in AL.4' holds only for the formal Euler product. AL.4 (read) defines Euler factors from Satake classes of unramified representations of (linear) groups and proves convergence 'where a supplied eigenvalue bound ensures it'. For Mp_2n the class is the ψ-relative parameter of item rmk-5-3 (missing, route 1). The second sentence, Yamana's holomorphy for Re s > n + 1 (Invent. Math. 196, Th. 9.1), is planned by no stage (an atlas search for Yamana or doubling finds nothing relevant). Recommend splitting it off as missing under route 1, next to prop-3-1, which uses it.

items.name: The Weil representation of Mp_2n × O(V)
items.statement: For F local and ψ a nontrivial additive character of F, (Mp_2n, O(V)) is a reductive dual pair and ω_ψ is the Weil representation of Mp_2n × O(V) with respect to ψ. For F a number field and ψ a nontrivial character of F\A, ω_ψ is the Weil representation of Mp_2n(A) × O(V)(A), and for f ∈ ω_ψ the theta function θ(f)(g, h) is a slowly increasing function on Sp_2n(F)\Mp_2n(A) × O(V)(F)\O(V)(A).
items.note: MP.2 gives the explicit formulas, MP.3 the dual-pair embeddings and splittings (odd-dimensional V gives a genuine action of Mp_2n), MP.4 the adelic Weil representation and MP.5 theta series and their growth. Review note: Planned is right: MP.2 (explicit formulas), MP.3 (dual-pair splittings, genuine action for odd-dimensional V), MP.4 (adelic Weil representation) and MP.5 (theta series, moderate growth).

items.name: Big and small theta lifts
items.statement: For π ∈ Irr Mp_2n, the maximal π-isotypic quotient of ω_ψ has the form π ⊠ Θ_ψ(π) for a smooth representation Θ_ψ(π) of O(V); θ_ψ(π) is its unique irreducible quotient when Θ_ψ(π) ≠ 0 (Howe duality), regarded as a representation of SO(V) by restriction, which stays irreducible by (2.1). Θ_ψ(σ̃) and θ_ψ(σ̃) are defined in the same way for σ̃ ∈ Irr O(V).
items.note: MP.3 defines big theta modules by coinvariants and small theta quotients 'when justified'. The justification is Howe duality (item howe-duality). Review note: MP.3 plans big theta modules (coinvariants) and small theta quotients 'when justified'. The justification is howe-duality (missing, route 2).

items.name: Howe duality
items.statement: Let F be a local field of characteristic zero. For π ∈ Irr Mp_2n with Θ_ψ(π) ≠ 0, Θ_ψ(π) has a unique irreducible quotient θ_ψ(π), and θ_ψ(π) ≅ θ_ψ(π′) ≠ 0 implies π ≅ π′; likewise for O(V) (Howe, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 2 (1989), archimedean; Waldspurger, p ≠ 2; Gan–Takeda, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 29 (2016), in general).
items.note: Used to define θ_ψ and for the injectivity in Remark 3.2, Proposition 4.4 and Lemma 6.9. MP.3 says a full Howe-duality theorem in all residual characteristics is 'a separately source-qualified extension'; Gan–Takeda is that source. Review note: Missing is right: MP.3 calls full Howe duality 'a separately source-qualified extension'. p. 974 prints only the uniqueness of the irreducible quotient. The injectivity half is part of the cited theorems [35], [90], [26], and it is what Remark 3.2 ('Theorem 2.1 and the Howe duality') and Corollary 4.2 use, so the item is right to include it.

items.name: The conservation relation and θ_ψ(σ) for SO(V)
items.statement: Let dim V = 2r + 1 with r ≥ n, and σ ∈ Irr SO(V). There is at most one extension σ̃ of σ to O(V) = SO(V) × {±1} with θ_ψ(σ̃) ≠ 0 on Mp_2n (Sun–Zhu, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 28 (2015)). If it exists one puts θ_ψ(σ) = θ_ψ(σ̃); otherwise θ_ψ(σ) = 0.
items.note: This is how theta lifts from SO(V), rather than O(V), to Mp_2n are defined throughout the paper. Review note: Missing is right; no stage plans Sun–Zhu. Check of the consequence: Sun–Zhu's relation for O(V) with dim V = 2r + 1 says that the first-occurrence ranks of σ̃ and σ̃ ⊗ det in the Mp_2n tower sum to 2r + 1. If both lifted to Mp_2n with n ≤ r, the sum would be ≤ 2n < 2r + 1, which proves 'at most one' and shows why r ≥ n is assumed. A formalization should state that relation itself, since the item states only its consequence.

items.name: The theta correspondence for unramified representations
items.statement: Let F be nonarchimedean of odd residual characteristic, ψ of order zero, K = Sp_2n(O) ⊂ Mp_2n via the standard splitting, and V split of dimension 2r + 1 with r ≥ n. Let π ∈ Irr Mp_2n be unramified, i.e., the unramified subquotient of Ind_B̃^{Mp_2n}(χ_ψ|·|^{s_1} ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ χ_ψ|·|^{s_n}) (5.5). Then θ_ψ(π) ≠ 0, and θ_ψ(π) (restricted to SO(V) = SO_2r+1) is the unramified representation with L-parameter ⊕_{i=1}^n (|·|^{s_i} ⊕ |·|^{−s_i}) ⊕ ⊕_{j=1}^{2r−2n} |·|^{r−n+1/2−j}. For r = n this says that the L-parameter ϕ of π relative to ψ is ⊕_i (|·|^{s_i} ⊕ |·|^{−s_i}) (Remark 5.3). For every r ≥ n, the L-parameter of θ_ψ(π) is ϕ ⊕ ⊕_{j=1}^{2r−2n} |·|^{r−n+1/2−j} (3.2). Conversely, the unramified representation of SO_2r+1 with L-parameter ϕ ⊕ ⊕_j |·|^{r−n+1/2−j} is θ_ψ(π) for the unramified π with ψ-relative parameter ϕ ((4.4) in the proof of Corollary 4.2).
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 3.1, (3.2); proof of Corollary 4.2; Remark 5.3, pp. 977–989 (arXiv v3 pp. 10–20)
items.note: Cited throughout as 'the local theta correspondence for unramified representations', with no reference. Routed to MP.3 as in PAPER-CHENEVIER-TAIBI-20 (item rallis-unramified). Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18): statement corrected against the paper: Minor. The item leaves implicit that θ_ψ(π) ≠ 0, which the proofs of Proposition 3.1 and Corollary 4.2 use. It also phrases the r = n case ('for r = n it is ϕ') as if ϕ were known independently, whereas the ψ-relative parameter of an unramified π is itself computed by this correspondence (Remark 5.3). Stating it with Satake data removes the apparent circularity and covers the converse used in (4.4). Review note: Missing is right: MP.3 plans no unramified computation. Route 2 agrees with PAPER-CHENEVIER-TAIBI-20.

items.name: Kudla's induction principle
items.statement: Let F be a local field of characteristic zero and ψ a nontrivial additive character of F. Let W_0 be a symplectic space of dimension 2n_0 and V_0 a quadratic space of odd dimension with trivial discriminant. Put W = W_0 ⊕ H^k (dimension 2n, n = n_0 + k) and V = V_0 ⊕ H^k. Let P̃ ⊂ Mp(W) be the preimage of the parabolic subgroup with Levi component GL_k × Sp(W_0), and Q ⊂ O(V) the parabolic subgroup with Levi component GL_k × O(V_0). Suppose π_0 ∈ Irr Mp(W_0) and σ̃_0 ∈ Irr O(V_0) satisfy Hom_{Mp(W_0)×O(V_0)}(ω_{ψ,W_0,V_0}, π_0 ⊗ σ̃_0) ≠ 0. Then for every irreducible representation τ of GL_k(F) there is a nonzero Mp(W) × O(V)-equivariant map ω_{ψ,W,V} → Ind_{P̃}^{Mp(W)}(τ̃_ψ ⊗ π_0) ⊗ Ind_Q^{O(V)}(τ ⊗ σ̃_0). Here induction is normalized and τ̃_ψ = τ ⊗ χ_ψ. For F archimedean the statement is for Harish-Chandra modules, or for Casselman–Wallach representations with the completed tensor product. Restricting to SO(V) through O(V) = SO(V) × {±1} gives the form used in the proof of Lemma 6.3. Sources: Kudla, Invent. Math. 83 (1986), which gives the p-adic Jacquet-module computations and Th. 2.5; Adams–Barbasch, J. Funct. Anal. 132, Cor. 3.21, for complex groups; Adams–Barbasch, Compos. Math. 113, Th. 8.4, for real groups.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 6.3, p. 992 (arXiv v3 p. 21)
items.note: The paper says the principle 'easily extends to the case at hand' and gives no argument (sourceIssues E2). Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18): statement corrected against the paper: Three problems. (1) The hypothesis should be that π_0 ⊗ σ̃_0 is a quotient of the Weil representation of the smaller pair (Mp_2n0, O(V_0)); 'correspond under the theta correspondence' presupposes Howe duality, which the principle does not need. (2) The local field (any, of characteristic zero), the sizes (n = n_0 + k, dim V = dim V_0 + 2k, V_0 of any odd dimension) and the category (Harish-Chandra modules or Casselman–Wallach representations when F is archimedean) are not stated. (3) The principle does not involve the stable range, temperedness or A-packets. The cited Adams–Barbasch, Compos. Math. 113, Th. 8.4 ('Induction Principle I') is stated for (O(p, q), Mp(2n, R)) 'with no further restrictions' on p, q, n, and for any Levi representations σ ⊗ σ′ that are quotients of the Levi Weil representation ω_M (checked in the authors' preprint, §8). Review note: The status 'missing' is right. MP.3 plans Jacquet filtrations and the elementary equivariance of the local theta modules, but it does not name the induction principle; MP.3 (route 2) is the natural owner. E2 is rejected (see issues). MP.3 should plan the principle in the general form above, not as an open proof obligation, and the route-1 brief's third 'proof obligation' should be dropped. For p-adic F the proof has three steps: a Levi-equivariant surjection ω ↠ ω_M ν obtained from a mixed model (Adams–Barbasch Lemmas 8.5–8.6, 'same as the proof of' their complex Prop. 3.13); a nonzero GL_k × GL_k-map S(M_k(F)) → τ ⊗ τ^∨ (a Godement–Jacquet zeta integral, or its leading coefficient at a pole); and Frobenius reciprocity.

items.name: The MVW involution and contragredients
items.statement: Let F be a local field of characteristic zero and δ ∈ GSp_2n(F) an element with similitude factor −1 (for instance δ = diag(1_n, −1_n)). Conjugation by δ lifts to an automorphism of Mp_2n, the MVW involution π ↦ π^δ. For every irreducible genuine representation π of Mp_2n, π^δ ≅ π^∨ (Mœglin–Vignéras–Waldspurger, LNM 1291, for F nonarchimedean; B. Sun, Pacific J. Math. 249 (2011), for F archimedean). Take δ diagonal. Then it normalizes the standard parabolic P̃ with Levi G̃L_k ×_{μ_2} Mp_2n0 and acts on Mp_2n0 as the MVW involution, and the lifted automorphism carries χ_ψ^{−1} to χ_ψ on G̃L_k. Hence, for τ ∈ Irr GL_k and π_0 ∈ Irr Mp_2n0, the contragredient of Ind_P̃((τ^∨ ⊗ χ_ψ) ⊗ π_0), namely Ind_P̃((τ ⊗ χ_ψ^{−1}) ⊗ π_0^∨), is carried by δ to Ind_P̃((τ ⊗ χ_ψ) ⊗ π_0). In particular, a surjection Ind_P̃((τ^∨ ⊗ χ_ψ) ⊗ π_0) ↠ π′ onto an irreducible π′ gives an injection π′ ↪ Ind_P̃(τ̃_ψ ⊗ π_0).
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 5.2, p. 989 (arXiv v3 p. 19)
items.note: Only the consequence displayed is used, in the included proof of the nonarchimedean case of Lemma 5.2. Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18): statement corrected against the paper: The item does not say what the MVW involution is. It also states the consequence without the compatibility with parabolic induction and with χ_ψ that the consequence rests on. Review note: 'Missing' is confirmed: MP.3's description (read) contains no MVW involution or contragredient statement. Route 2 is appropriate.

items.name: Kudla's filtration of the Jacquet modules of ω_ψ
items.statement: Let F be nonarchimedean, W a 2n-dimensional symplectic space, V a (2n+1)-dimensional quadratic space and Ω = ω_{ψ,V,W}. Let Y_k ⊂ V be a k-dimensional isotropic subspace with V = Y_k ⊕ V_{n−k} ⊕ Y_k^*, and let Q(Y_k) ⊂ O(V) be its stabilizer, with Levi M(Y_k) = GL(Y_k) × O(V_{n−k}). The normalized Jacquet module R_{Q(Y_k)}(Ω) has an M(Y_k) × Mp(W)-invariant filtration 0 ⊂ R^k ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ R^1 ⊂ R^0 = R_{Q(Y_k)}(Ω). For 0 ≤ r ≤ k its successive quotients are R^r/R^{r+1} ≅ Ind^{GL(Y_k)×O(V_{n−k})×Mp(W)}_{Q(Y_{k−r},Y_k)×O(V_{n−k})×P̃(X_r)} (S(Isom(Y′_r, X_r)) ⊗ Ω_{V_{n−k},W_{n−r},ψ}). Here Q(Y_{k−r}, Y_k) ⊂ GL(Y_k) is the parabolic with Levi GL(Y_{k−r}) × GL(Y′_r), and P̃(X_r) ⊂ Mp(W) is the preimage of the stabilizer of an r-dimensional isotropic X_r ⊂ W, W = X_r ⊕ W_{n−r} ⊕ X_r^*. GL(Y_{k−r}) acts by |det|^{(k−r)/2}; GL(Y′_r) × GL(X_r) acts on S(Isom(Y′_r, X_r)) by (b, c)f(t) = f(c^{−1} t b), the regular representation of GL_r × GL_r on S(GL_r); and O(V_{n−k}) × Mp(W_{n−r}) acts by the Weil representation (Kudla, Invent. Math. 83 (1986), Th. 2.8; Gan–Savin, Compos. Math. 148 (2012), Prop. 7.3). Consequence (Gan–Savin, Lemma 7.4, stated there for s ≥ 0; its proof gives it for every s > −1/2). Let τ be a unitary square-integrable representation of GL(Y_k), s > −1/2 and σ_1 a representation of O(V_{n−k}). Then Hom_{M(Y_k)}(R^r/R^{r+1}, τ|det|^{−s} ⊠ σ_1) = 0 for every r < k. Indeed, the centre of GL(Y_{k−r}) acts on |det|^{−s} R_{Q(Y_{k−r},Y_k)}(τ) through exponents of real part −s + t_1 < 1/2, where t_1 ≤ 0, and on R^r/R^{r+1} by |det|^{(k−r)/2}, where (k−r)/2 ≥ 1/2. Hence Hom_{M(Y_k)}(R_{Q(Y_k)}(Ω), τ|det|^{−s} ⊠ σ_1) embeds in Hom_{M(Y_k)}(R^k, τ|det|^{−s} ⊠ σ_1).

items.note: MP.3 plans 'Jacquet filtrations'. The surjection the paper derives from the filtration and Gan–Savin's Lemma 7.4 is part of item lemma-5-2 (sourceIssues E1). Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18): statement corrected against the paper: 'For a maximal parabolic subgroup of O(V) (or of Mp_2n) with Levi factor GL_k × O(V_0)' is garbled: a maximal parabolic of Mp_2n has Levi G̃L_k × Mp_2n−2k. The item also leaves the successive quotients unspecified. The proof of Lemma 5.2 needs the explicit equal-rank form (Gan–Savin, Prop. 7.3) together with the vanishing statement of Gan–Savin's Lemma 7.4, extended to s > −1/2 (see issue E1). Review note: MP.3 (read) plans 'Jacquet filtrations', with Kudla's 1996 notes as source. 'Planned' is right for the filtration. The vanishing consequence is a one-line central-character comparison and belongs with it.

items.name: The local Shimura correspondence
items.statement: Let F be a local field of characteristic zero and ψ a nontrivial additive character of F. For each (2n+1)-dimensional quadratic space V over F with trivial discriminant, let θ_ψ be the theta lift for the equal-rank dual pair (Mp_2n, O(V)), regarded between Mp_2n and SO(V) as in item conservation-relation. Then θ_ψ is a bijection Irr Mp_2n → ⊔_V Irr SO(V), the union over isometry classes of such V; for F nonarchimedean the target is Irr SO(V⁺) ⊔ Irr SO(V⁻), and every π has a nonzero lift to exactly one V (Gan–Savin, Compos. Math. 148 (2012), for F nonarchimedean; Adams–Barbasch, J. Funct. Anal. 132 (1995), for F = C, and Compos. Math. 113 (1998), for F = R). θ_ψ preserves square-integrability and temperedness, preserves genericity of tempered representations, and preserves L- and ε-factors, Plancherel measures and formal degrees (Gan–Ichino, Invent. Math. 195). For F nonarchimedean it is compatible with parabolic induction as follows (Gan–Savin, Th. 8.1, with Gan–Takeda's Howe duality when the residual characteristic is 2). (i) If σ_0 ∈ Irr SO(V_0) is tempered, dim V_0 = 2n_0 + 1, and its big theta lift Θ_ψ(σ_0) to Mp_2n0 is nonzero, then Θ_ψ(σ_0) is irreducible, so Θ_ψ(σ_0) = θ_ψ(σ_0). (ii) If a tempered σ ∈ Irr SO(V) lies in Ind_Q(τ_1 ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ τ_r ⊗ σ_0), with τ_i unitary square-integrable and σ_0 square-integrable, then Θ_ψ(σ) ⊂ Ind_P̃(τ̃_{1,ψ} ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ τ̃_{r,ψ} ⊗ Θ_ψ(σ_0)). (iii) If π = J_P̃(τ̃_{1,ψ}|det|^{s_1} ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ τ̃_{r,ψ}|det|^{s_r} ⊗ π_0) is a Langlands quotient (τ_i tempered, s_1 > ⋯ > s_r > 0, π_0 tempered), then θ_ψ(π) is the Langlands quotient J_Q(τ_1|det|^{s_1} ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ τ_r|det|^{s_r} ⊗ θ_ψ(π_0)) of SO(V), V = H^k ⊕ V_0. The same holds with the roles of Mp_2n and SO(V) exchanged.
items.note: The last sentence is used in the proof of Lemma 5.2 ('Θ_ψ(σ_0) = θ_ψ(σ_0) = π_0 by [24]'). Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18): statement corrected against the paper: (a) The last sentence ('For tempered σ_0, Θ_ψ(σ_0) = θ_ψ(σ_0)') is stated for every F. The paper asserts and uses it only for F nonarchimedean, in the proof of Lemma 5.2 ('by [24]', i.e. Gan–Savin Th. 8.1(ii), with Howe duality in residual characteristic 2). (b) 'Compatible with R-groups / with the Langlands classification' is too vague for how the proof of Lemma 5.2 uses it. That proof needs the precise form: θ_ψ of a Langlands quotient is the Langlands quotient with the same GL-data (Gan–Savin Th. 8.1(iii)). Review note: 'Missing' is confirmed: no stage plans the theta correspondence as a bijection; MP.3 plans theta modules only. Route 1 fits.

items.name: The local Langlands correspondence for split SO_2n+1
items.statement: For F local of characteristic zero (Arthur), Irr SO_2n+1(F) = ⊔_φ Π_φ(SO_2n+1), the union over equivalence classes of L-parameters φ : L_F → Sp_2n(C), with Π_φ(SO_2n+1) in bijection with the characters η of S_φ with η(z_φ) = 1 (F nonarchimedean or C). σ ∈ Π_φ is square-integrable if and only if φ is good and multiplicity-free, and tempered if and only if φ is tempered. For φ = ϕ ⊕ ϕ^∨ ⊕ φ_0 as in (5.2), σ_η is an irreducible subquotient of Ind_Q^{SO_2n+1}(τ ⊗ σ_{η_0}), and for tempered φ the packet consists of the irreducible summands of these induced representations.
items.note: Arthur's book; for real groups the correspondence is Langlands–Shelstad. The Vogan-packet version over all V is item llc-so-inner. Review note: ML.4 (read) plans the packets and multiplicities of Arthur's classification, so 'planned' is right. The real case rests on Shelstad's tempered theory, which Arthur imports.

items.name: The local Langlands correspondence for SO(V) over all V (Vogan packets)
items.statement: Let F be local of characteristic zero. For each V there is a partition Irr SO(V) = ⊔_φ Π_φ(SO(V)), and there are bijections ⊔_V Π_φ(SO(V)) ↔ Ŝ_φ, σ_η ↔ η (5.3). The first union runs over equivalence classes of 2n-dimensional symplectic representations φ of L_F, the second over isometry classes of (2n+1)-dimensional quadratic spaces V over F with trivial discriminant (Langlands and Shelstad for F = R; Arthur for SO(V⁺); Mœglin–Renard, arXiv:1803.07662, for SO(V⁻)). A σ ∈ Π_φ(SO(V)) is square-integrable if and only if φ is good and multiplicity-free, and tempered if and only if φ is tempered. Let Ŝ_{φ,V} be the set of η for which σ_η is a representation of SO(V). Then Ŝ_{φ,V} ⊂ {η ∈ Ŝ_φ | η(z_φ) = ε(V)}, where ε(V) is the normalized Hasse–Witt invariant, with equality when F is nonarchimedean or F = C (where S_φ = 0). Write φ = ϕ ⊕ ϕ^∨ ⊕ φ_0 as in (5.2), with k = dim ϕ. Then Π_φ(SO(V)) = ∅ unless the F-rank of SO(V) is at least k. In that case V = H^k ⊕ V_0 with V_0 of dimension 2n_0 + 1 and trivial discriminant. Let Q ⊂ SO(V) be a parabolic subgroup with Levi GL_k × SO(V_0) and τ ∈ Irr GL_k the representation corresponding to ϕ. For η ∈ Ŝ_{φ,V}, let η_0 be η regarded as a character of S_{φ_0} = S_φ. Then σ_η is an irreducible subquotient of Ind_Q^{SO(V)}(τ ⊗ σ_{η_0}), with σ_{η_0} ∈ Π_{φ_0}(SO(V_0)). If φ is tempered, Π_φ(SO(V)) consists of the irreducible summands of the representations Ind_Q^{SO(V)}(τ ⊗ σ_0), σ_0 ∈ Π_{φ_0}(SO(V_0)).
items.note: ML.4 names Arthur, Mok and Kaletha–Minguez–Shin–White but not the odd orthogonal inner forms. Mœglin–Renard (arXiv:1803.07662; LNM 2221) give the full tempered classification for non-quasi-split groups in the p-adic case. Ishimoto (IMRN 2024, Th. 3.14) proves the local classification with the local intertwining relation and the endoscopic character relations for generic parameters. Routed to ML.4 as PAPER-CHENEVIER-TAIBI-20 routed Mœglin–Renard. Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18): statement corrected against the paper: The item uses Q, τ, η_0 and σ_{η_0} without introducing them, and does not name ε(V). It also omits the tempered-case description (the packet consists of the irreducible summands of the induced representations), which the proof of Lemma 5.1 uses. Review note: 'Missing' is confirmed: ML.4 names Arthur, Mok and KMSW, not the odd orthogonal inner forms. Route 3 is appropriate.

items.name: Symplectic, good, tempered and almost tempered parameters; S_φ and z_φ
items.statement: Let F be a local field of characteristic zero. L_F is the Weil group W_F if F is archimedean and the Weil–Deligne group W_F × SL_2(C) if F is nonarchimedean. Its representations are finite-dimensional, continuous and semisimple on W_F, and algebraic on SL_2(C). An n-dimensional representation φ is symplectic if it preserves a nondegenerate alternating bilinear form on C^n, and tempered if φ(W_F) is relatively compact in GL_n(C); an irreducible symplectic φ is tempered. Regard a 2n-dimensional symplectic φ as φ : L_F → Sp_2n(C) and write φ = ⊕_i m_i φ_i (5.1), with m_i ≥ 1 and pairwise distinct irreducible φ_i. Then φ is good if every φ_i is symplectic; multiplicity-free if every m_i = 1; tempered if every φ_i is tempered; and almost tempered if for every i there is s_i ∈ R with |s_i| < 1/2 such that φ_i|·|^{−s_i} is tempered. A good φ is tempered. For a generic elliptic A-parameter φ of Mp_2n over a number field, every localization φ_v is almost tempered (Jacquet–Shalika bound). Every such φ decomposes as φ = ϕ ⊕ ϕ^∨ ⊕ φ_0 (5.2), where ϕ is k-dimensional with no symplectic irreducible summand, φ_0 = ⊕_{i∈I_0} m_i φ_i (I_0 = {i | φ_i symplectic}) is good of dimension 2n_0, and k + n_0 = n. The component group S_φ of the centralizer of φ(L_F) in Sp_2n(C) is ⊕_{i∈I_0} (Z/2Z)a_i (a_i ↔ φ_i), the image of −1 is z_φ = Σ_{i∈I_0} m_i a_i, and S_{φ_0} = S_φ.
items.note: 'Almost tempered' for localizations of global generic parameters uses the bound |s_i| < 1/2 on the exponents of local components of unitary cuspidal representations of GL_{n_i} (Jacquet–Shalika), which the paper uses without citation. Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18): statement corrected against the paper: The item uses 'symplectic', 'tempered' and 'multiplicity-free' without defining them; items llc-so-inner and llc-mp also use 'multiplicity-free'. It does not say what L_F and its representations are. The almost-temperedness of localizations rests on the Jacquet–Shalika bound, which no item covers (a new item is proposed in coverage). Review note: 'Missing' is correct; route 1.

items.name: The local Langlands correspondence for Mp_2n relative to ψ
items.statement: Composing θ_ψ with the local Langlands correspondence for the groups SO(V) gives a partition Irr Mp_2n = ⊔_φ Π_{φ,ψ}(Mp_2n) over equivalence classes of 2n-dimensional symplectic representations φ of L_F, and bijections Π_{φ,ψ}(Mp_2n) ↔ Ŝ_φ, π_η ↔ η ((1.2), (5.4)), which depend on ψ as described in Gan–Savin, Th. 12.1. π ∈ Π_{φ,ψ} is square-integrable if and only if φ is good and multiplicity-free, and tempered if and only if φ is tempered. For φ = ϕ ⊕ ϕ^∨ ⊕ φ_0, P ⊂ Sp_2n with Levi GL_k × Sp_2n0 and τ ↔ ϕ, π_η is an irreducible subquotient of Ind_P̃^{Mp_2n}(τ̃_ψ ⊗ π_{η_0}); for tempered φ, Π_{φ,ψ}(Mp_2n) consists of the irreducible summands of Ind_P̃^{Mp_2n}(τ̃_ψ ⊗ π_0), π_0 ∈ Π_{φ_0,ψ}(Mp_2n0).
items.note: §1.5: the packets are defined through θ_ψ, so the endoscopic character relations are not known a priori. They were proved by Adams and Renard for F = R, and by Luo (J. reine angew. Math. 768 (2020)) for F nonarchimedean, using W.-W. Li's stable trace formula for Mp_2n and this paper's main result.

items.name: Parabolic induction on Mp_2n and the character χ_ψ
items.statement: For a parabolic subgroup P = MN of Sp_2n with M ≅ ∏_i GL_{k_i} × Sp_2n0, P̃ and M̃ are the preimages of P and M in Mp_2n (locally or adelically). For τ ∈ Irr GL_k, τ̃_ψ = τ ⊗ χ_ψ is its twist by the genuine quartic character χ_ψ of the two-fold cover of GL_k (Gan–Ichino, Invent. Math. 195, §2.6), and genuine irreducible representations of M̃ have the form (⊗_i τ̃_{i,ψ}) ⊗ π_0. Globally χ_ψ is the genuine quartic automorphic character of the cover of GL_{k_i}(A).
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 4.1 and §5.3, pp. 979–988 (arXiv v3 pp. 12–19)
items.note: MP.3 plans the splitting characters of dual pairs but not parabolic subgroups of the cover or χ_ψ. SR.2 plans induction and Jacquet functors for linear groups; the paper also uses the analogous adelic induction Ind_{P̃(A)}^{Mp_2n(A)}. Review note: 'Missing' is confirmed. SR.2 (read) supplies smooth and normalized induction from closed subgroups, and MP.2 computes the Weil representation on Levi elements. Neither plans the preimages P̃, M̃ = G̃L_{k_1} ×_{μ_2} ⋯ ×_{μ_2} Mp_2n0, the description of their genuine representations, or χ_ψ. Route 1 should build them on top of SR.2 and MP.2.

items.name: Lemma 5.1 (irreducibility for SO(V))
items.statement: Let φ = ϕ ⊕ ϕ^∨ ⊕ φ_0 be almost tempered, V = H^k ⊕ V_0, Q ⊂ SO(V) a parabolic subgroup with Levi GL_k × SO(V_0) and τ ∈ Irr GL_k associated to ϕ. Then Ind_Q^{SO(V)}(τ ⊗ σ_0) is irreducible for every σ_0 ∈ Π_{φ_0}(SO(V_0)).
items.note: Proof: for tempered φ, the bijectivity of (5.3) and S_{φ_0} = S_φ. Otherwise, by induction in stages, the case 0 < |s_i| < 1/2 with σ_0 tempered: Speh–Vogan for F archimedean; for F nonarchimedean, Mœglin–Waldspurger (Astérisque 347, §2.14) together with the conjecture of Gross–Prasad and Rallis, proved in Gan–Ichino, Invent. Math. 206, App. B. Review note: 'Missing' is correct; route 3 (ML.4) as a source is appropriate. The tempered step uses the refined inductive property (the summands of Ind_Q(τ ⊗ σ_{η_0}) are the σ_η with η ↦ η_0), which is part of Arthur's local theory, so it is not a gap.

items.name: Lemma 5.2 (irreducibility for Mp_2n)
items.statement: Let F be local of characteristic zero and ψ a nontrivial additive character of F. Let φ be a 2n-dimensional almost tempered symplectic representation of L_F, written φ = ϕ ⊕ ϕ^∨ ⊕ φ_0 as in (5.2) with k = dim ϕ. Let P ⊂ Sp_2n be a parabolic subgroup with Levi GL_k × Sp_2n0 and P̃ its preimage in Mp_2n, let τ ∈ Irr GL_k correspond to ϕ, and put τ̃_ψ = τ ⊗ χ_ψ. Then Ind_P̃^{Mp_2n}(τ̃_ψ ⊗ π_0) is irreducible for every π_0 ∈ Π_{φ_0,ψ}(Mp_2n0).
items.note: For tempered φ this follows from the bijectivity of (5.4). Otherwise, by induction in stages, τ has exponents 0 < |s_i| < 1/2 and π_0 is tempered. F = C: Speh–Vogan. F = R: Gan–Ichino, Tunisian J. Math. 1 (2019). F nonarchimedean: Atobe, Math. Ann. 371, Th. 3.13. The paper also includes a proof for F nonarchimedean: σ = Ind_Q^{SO(V)}(τ ⊗ θ_ψ(π_0)) is irreducible by Lemma 5.1 and equals θ_ψ(π′) for the Langlands quotient π′; Kudla's filtration and Gan–Savin's Lemma 7.4 give a surjection Ind_P̃((τ^∨ ⊗ χ_ψ) ⊗ π_0) ↠ π′; the MVW involution gives π′ ↪ Ind_P̃(τ̃_ψ ⊗ π_0); and π′ occurs in the standard module only once (Ban–Jantzen). That proof applies Gan–Savin's Lemma 7.4 for s > −1/2 without argument (sourceIssues E1). Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18): statement corrected against the paper: The lemma is stated without its setting: P, P̃, τ and τ̃_ψ are defined only in item llc-mp. The note's remark that the included proof applies Gan–Savin's Lemma 7.4 for s > −1/2 'without argument' should be dropped or reworded. The extension is immediate from Gan–Savin's proof, and E1 is rejected (see issues). Review note: 'Missing' is correct; route 1.

items.name: The Langlands quotient theorem for finite central covers
items.statement: Let F be nonarchimedean and G̃ a finite central extension of a connected reductive group over F, for example Mp_2n. Take a standard parabolic P̃ = M̃N, an irreducible tempered genuine representation σ of M̃, and ν in the open positive chamber of a_M^*. The standard module Ind_P̃^{G̃}(σ ⊗ e^{⟨ν, H_M(·)⟩}) has a unique irreducible quotient, its Langlands quotient, and that quotient occurs in the standard module with multiplicity one. Every irreducible genuine representation is the Langlands quotient of a standard module whose data (P, σ, ν) are unique up to conjugacy (Ban–Jantzen, Glas. Mat. 48 (2013), Langlands quotient theorem and Remark 4.5). For Mp_2n the standard modules are Ind_P̃((τ_1|det|^{s_1} ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ τ_r|det|^{s_r}) ⊗ χ_ψ ⊗ π_0), with τ_i tempered representations of GL_{k_i}, s_1 > ⋯ > s_r > 0 and π_0 tempered genuine.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 5.2, p. 989 (arXiv v3 p. 19)
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18): statement corrected against the paper: The proof of Lemma 5.2 also uses the existence and uniqueness of the irreducible quotient of a standard module ('Let π′ be the unique irreducible quotient of π', p. 988). The item states only multiplicity one, and it does not say what a standard module of Mp_2n is. Review note: 'Missing' is confirmed: apart from ET.6's GL_m segment theory, no stage plans the Langlands classification of p-adic groups, linear or covering. Route 1 fits.

items.name: Remark 5.3 (unramified genuine representations)
items.statement: Let F be nonarchimedean of odd residual characteristic, ψ of order zero, and K = Sp_2n(O) ⊂ Mp_2n via the standard splitting. An irreducible genuine π with a nonzero K-fixed vector is the unique unramified subquotient of Ind_B̃^{Mp_2n}(χ_ψ|·|^{s_1} ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ χ_ψ|·|^{s_n}) (5.5) for some s_1, …, s_n ∈ C, and its L-parameter relative to ψ is ⊕_{i=1}^n (|·|^{s_i} ⊕ |·|^{−s_i}). (5.5) is irreducible if |Re s_i| < 1/2 for all i, and it is unitary if, for each i, either s_i ∈ √−1 R or s_i ∈ R with |s_i| < 1/2 (Lapid–Muić–Tadić, IMRN 2004, Lemma 3.3).
items.note: Irreducibility is shown in the proof of Lemma 5.2. The proof of Corollary 4.2 also uses that the unramified representations π_{φ_v} are unitary, citing Tadić's classification of the unitary dual of GL_n and this remark. Review note: 'Missing' is confirmed: SR.4 plans Satake only for unramified linear groups. For the use in Corollary 4.2, the unramified parameters of local components of unitary cuspidal φ_i can have exponents of the form it ± x (0 < x < 1/2), or x + πi/log q. The remark's criterion (s_i ∈ √−1R, or s_i ∈ R with |s_i| < 1/2) does not cover these literally. Unitarity then follows from Tadić's classification [86] together with unitary induction through G̃L_2 blocks, and from the remark applied with ψ_u for u a nonsquare unit. The paper's 'see [86] and Remark 5.3' covers this; the item's note should say it.

items.name: Arthur's local A-packets of SO_2r+1
items.statement: Let F be local of characteristic zero. Let φ′ : L_F × SL_2(C) → Sp_2r(C) be a local A-parameter, S_φ′ the component group of the centralizer of its image, z_φ′ the image of −1 and S̄_φ′ = S_φ′/⟨z_φ′⟩. Arthur attaches to φ′ the packet Π_φ′(SO_2r+1) = {σ_η′ | η′ ∈ (S̄_φ′)^}, where each σ_η′ is a possibly zero, possibly reducible semisimple representation of SO_2r+1(F) of finite length. If φ′ is generic (trivial on SL_2(C)), Π_φ′ is the L-packet of φ′; if moreover F is nonarchimedean or F = C, every σ_η′ is nonzero and irreducible. The L-parameter associated to φ′ is ϕ_φ′(w) = φ′(w, diag(|w|^{1/2}, |w|^{−1/2})) (5.6). Inductive property (§5.4): let φ′ = φ ⊕ S_{2r−2n}, where φ is a 2n-dimensional symplectic representation of L_F and 2n < r − 1. Write φ = ϕ ⊕ ϕ^∨ ⊕ φ_0 as in (5.2) with k = dim ϕ, and put φ′_0 = φ_0 ⊕ S_{2r−2n}. Let Q′ ⊂ SO_2r+1 be a parabolic subgroup with Levi GL_k × SO_2r−2k+1 and τ ∈ Irr GL_k the representation corresponding to ϕ. Then for every η′ ∈ (S̄_φ′)^, σ_η′ is the semisimplification of Ind_Q′^{SO_2r+1}(τ ⊗ σ_{η′_0}), where η′_0 is η′ regarded as a character of S̄_φ′_0 = S̄_φ′. By Arthur, Prop. 7.4.1, the member of the L-packet Π_{ϕ_φ′}(SO_2r+1) attached to the trivial character of S_{ϕ_φ′} is a summand of the member of Π_φ′ attached to the trivial character of S̄_φ′.
items.locator: §4.3, §5.4 and proofs of Lemmas 6.4, 6.8, 6.11, pp. 981–998 (arXiv v3 pp. 13–27)
items.note: Arthur gives no explicit description of σ_η′ for non-generic φ′; the paper uses Mœglin's explicit construction for the properties it needs (items lemma-5-5 and prop-5-4). Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18): statement corrected against the paper: The inductive property is stated for an arbitrary 'φ′ = ϕ ⊕ ϕ^∨ ⊕ φ′_0' without its hypotheses, and Q′ and τ are never introduced. The paper states it only when φ′ = φ ⊕ S_{2r−2n} with 2n < r − 1, ϕ comes from the decomposition (5.2) of the L_F-representation φ, and φ′_0 = φ_0 ⊕ S_{2r−2n} (p. 990). The item also omits the §4.3 statement that, for generic φ′ with F nonarchimedean or complex, every σ_η′ is nonzero and irreducible. That statement fails in general for F = R, where σ_η′ can be zero. Review note: ML.4 (read) plans Arthur's packets, so 'planned' is right. Mœglin's explicit construction, which the paper cites for non-generic φ′, is not named in ML.4.

items.name: Lemma 5.5 (irreducibility for A-packets of SO_2r+1)
items.statement: Let φ′ = φ ⊕ S_{2r−2n} with φ a 2n-dimensional almost tempered symplectic representation of L_F, 2n < r − 1, φ = ϕ ⊕ ϕ^∨ ⊕ φ_0 and φ′_0 = φ_0 ⊕ S_{2r−2n}. Then Ind_Q′^{SO_2r+1}(τ ⊗ σ′_0) is irreducible for every irreducible subrepresentation σ′_0 of every representation in the A-packet Π_{φ′_0}(SO_2r−2k+1), where Q′ ⊂ SO_2r+1 is a parabolic subgroup with Levi GL_k × SO_2r−2k+1 and τ ∈ Irr GL_k is associated to ϕ.
items.note: Proved in greater generality by Mœglin ('Multiplicité 1 dans les paquets d'Arthur aux places p-adiques', §3.2; Adv. Math. 228 (2011), Prop. 5.1) for F nonarchimedean, and by Mœglin–Renard (Contemp. Math. 691, §6) for F = C. For F = R it is proved in Gan–Ichino, Tunisian J. Math. 1 (2019), by the Kazhdan–Lusztig algorithm, using that σ′_0 has half-integral infinitesimal character (Bergeron–Clozel, Invent. Math. 192, Lemme 3.4).

items.name: Proposition 5.4
items.statement: Let φ be a 2n-dimensional almost tempered symplectic representation of L_F and φ′ = φ ⊕ S_{2r−2n} with 2n < r − 1. Then σ_η′ is nonzero and irreducible for every η′ ∈ (S̄_φ′)^, and Π_φ′(SO_2r+1) is multiplicity-free, that is, the σ_η′ are pairwise distinct.
items.note: Largely due to Mœglin (F nonarchimedean), Mœglin and Mœglin–Renard (F = C), and Arancibia–Mœglin–Renard and Mœglin–Renard (F = R, φ good); Xu (Canad. J. Math. 69) expounds Mœglin's results. The paper proves it in §6 by theta lifts, together with Proposition 6.1. For F = R its proof uses the multiplicity formula (6.1) for non-split SO(V), which the paper assumes and Ishimoto later proved (item amf-nonsplit).

items.name: Elliptic A-parameters for Mp_2n and their localizations
items.statement: An elliptic A-parameter for Mp_2n is a formal unordered finite sum φ = ⊕_i φ_i ⊠ S_{d_i} (1.1), where φ_i is an irreducible self-dual cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_{n_i}(A) and S_{d_i} the d_i-dimensional irreducible representation of SL_2(C), such that Σ_i n_i d_i = 2n; φ_i is symplectic if d_i is odd and orthogonal if d_i is even; and (φ_i, d_i) = (φ_j, d_j) implies i = j. φ is generic if every d_i = 1. Its localization φ_v = ⊕_i φ_{i,v} ⊠ S_{d_i}, with φ_{i,v} regarded as a representation of L_{F_v} (the Weil group if v is archimedean, the Weil–Deligne group otherwise), is a local A-parameter L_{F_v} × SL_2(C) → Sp_2n(C) with L-parameter ϕ_{φ_v}(w) = φ_v(w, diag(|w|^{1/2}, |w|^{−1/2})).
items.note: These are exactly Arthur's elliptic A-parameters for SO_2n+1 ('elliptic A-parameters for SO(V) (or equivalently those for Mp_2r)', §3.1); PAPER-JIANG-ZHANG-20 marks Arthur's global parameters as planned in ML.4. What is new for Mp_2n is the ψ-relative localization of representations (items llc-mp, rmk-5-3). Review note: Planned in ML.4 is acceptable: these are Arthur's elliptic parameters for SO_2n+1. The meaning of 'symplectic/orthogonal' is item selfdual-types. The assertion that φ_v is a local A-parameter into Sp_2n(C) ('Note that φ_v gives rise to an A-parameter', p. 967) needs the local–global compatibility of the symplectic/orthogonal type of φ_i. No item covers it; see the coverage row.

items.name: Arthur's decomposition and multiplicity formula for split SO_2r+1
items.statement: Let F be a number field and SO_2r+1 split over F. (a) L²_disc(SO_2r+1) = ⊕_φ′ L²_φ′(SO_2r+1), the sum over elliptic A-parameters φ′ for SO_2r+1 (equivalently for Mp_2r), where L²_φ′(SO_2r+1) is a full near equivalence class of irreducible representations σ in L²_disc(SO_2r+1) such that the L-parameter of σ_v is ϕ_{φ′_v} for almost all v (Arthur; §3.1). (b) Write φ′ = ⊕_i φ_i ⊠ S_{d_i}. Let S_φ′ = ⊕_i (Z/2Z)a′_i, with a′_i ↔ φ_i ⊠ S_{d_i}, and S̄_φ′ = S_φ′/Δ(Z/2Z), where Δ(Z/2Z) = {0, Σ_i a′_i}. For each place v, let S_{φ′_v} be the component group of the centralizer of the image of φ′_v : L_{F_v} × SL_2(C) → Sp_2r(C), z_{φ′_v} the image of −1, and S̄_{φ′_v} = S_{φ′_v}/⟨z_{φ′_v}⟩. This gives canonical maps S̄_φ′ → S̄_{φ′_v}, the compact group S̄_{φ′,A} = ∏_v S̄_{φ′_v} and the diagonal map Δ : S̄_φ′ → S̄_{φ′,A}. Let Π_{φ′_v}(SO_2r+1) = {σ_{η′_v} | η′_v ∈ (S̄_{φ′_v})^} be Arthur's local A-packet, whose members are possibly zero, possibly reducible semisimple representations of finite length (the L-packet of φ′_v when φ′ is generic). For η′ = ⊗_v η′_v ∈ (S̄_{φ′,A})^, put σ_η′ = ⊗_v σ_{η′_v}, and let ε_φ′ be Arthur's quadratic character of S̄_φ′ ([6, (1.5.6)]). Then L²_φ′(SO_2r+1) ≅ ⊕_{η′} m_η′ σ_η′ as semisimple representations, with m_η′ = 1 if Δ*η′ = ε_φ′ and m_η′ = 0 otherwise (4.5) (Arthur, Th. 1.5.2).
items.note: Arthur's classification rests on Ngô's fundamental lemma and the stabilization of the twisted trace formula (Mœglin–Waldspurger); ML.4 owns these source dependencies. §3.1 notes that (a) is expected for non-split SO(V) too. Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18): statement corrected against the paper: Part (b) leaves out what σ_{η′_v} and S̄_{φ′_v} are (§4.3, p. 981). S̄_{φ′_v} = S_{φ′_v}/⟨z_{φ′_v}⟩, where z_{φ′_v} is the image of −1. The σ_{η′_v} are Arthur's A-packet members, which are possibly zero, possibly reducible semisimple representations of finite length. So σ_η′ is semisimple and (4.5) is an isomorphism of semisimple representations, not a sum of irreducibles. The item also does not say that Δ(Z/2Z) is {0, Σ_i a′_i}. Review note: Planned in ML.4 is right. The local-packet half overlaps item arthur-local-packets, which is consistent.

items.name: Arthur's multiplicity formula for non-split SO(V), generic parameters
items.statement: Hypothesis, assumed in the paper (Arthur's results extended to non-split SO(V)). Let F be a number field and V a (2m + 1)-dimensional quadratic space over F with trivial discriminant, for any m ≥ 0. (i) (§3.1, 'expected') L²_disc(SO(V)) = ⊕_Φ L²_Φ(SO(V)), the sum over elliptic A-parameters Φ for SO(V), where L²_Φ(SO(V)) is a full near equivalence class of irreducible representations Σ in L²_disc(SO(V)) such that the L-parameter of Σ_v is ϕ_{Φ_v} for almost all v. (ii) (6.1) Let Φ be a generic elliptic A-parameter for SO(V), with global component group S_Φ, canonical maps S_Φ → S_{Φ_v} and diagonal map Δ : S_Φ → S_{Φ,A}. For η = ⊗_v η_v ∈ Ŝ_{Φ,A} with η_v ∈ Ŝ_{Φ_v,V_v} for all v, put Σ_η = ⊗_v Σ_{η_v}, where Σ_{η_v} ∈ Π_{Φ_v}(SO(V_v)) corresponds to η_v under (5.3). Then L²_Φ(SO(V)) ≅ ⊕_η m_η Σ_η, the sum over continuous characters η of S_{Φ,A} with η_v ∈ Ŝ_{Φ_v,V_v} for all v, where m_η = 1 if Δ*η = 1 and m_η = 0 otherwise. In particular L²_Φ(SO(V)) is multiplicity-free and m_disc(Σ_η) = m_η. When SO(V) is split, (i) and (ii) are Arthur's theorem (item arthur-global-so).
items.note: The paper assumes (6.1) when SO(V) is not split ('which has not been established if SO(V) is nonsplit but will be assumed in this paper'); Theorem 1.4 is stated under this hypothesis. Ishimoto, 'The endoscopic classification of representations of non-quasi-split odd special orthogonal groups', IMRN 2024 (arXiv:2301.12143), proves it for generic parameters (Th. 3.14 with Th. 3.13), and says that the result of Gan–Ichino on the generic part 'will be unconditional'. ML.4 is told to 'preserve any source-specific conditional hypotheses until the exact missing result and applicable replacement are verified', which is this case. Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18): statement corrected against the paper: The first sentence states as a fact that L²_disc(SO(V)) decomposes into near equivalence classes L²_Φ(SO(V)) indexed by elliptic A-parameters. For non-split SO(V) the paper calls this decomposition 'expected' (§3.1, p. 977; §6.2, p. 993: 'Recall the (expected) decomposition') and assumes it together with (6.1): Theorem 1.4 is proved 'under the hypothesis that Arthur's result [6] extends to the case of nonsplit odd special orthogonal groups; see Sections 3.1 and 6.2' (p. 970). The item should present both parts as the hypothesis. The decomposition itself is used, not only (6.1). Lemma 6.10 proves Σ cuspidal 'from the argument in the proof of Proposition 4.1', and that argument needs weak lifts to GL of the cuspidal representations of SO(V_0)(A) on Levi subgroups GL × SO(V_0) of a possibly non-split SO(V). Review note: 'Missing' and the route to ML.4 (route 3) are right. ML.4 names Arthur, Mok and KMSW and asks that conditional hypotheses stay visible, but it plans no classification for non-quasi-split odd orthogonal groups. The arXiv abstract of Ishimoto (arXiv:2301.12143) states the classification for non-quasi-split odd SO 'for generic parameters', which covers (ii). Before Theorem 1.4 is recorded as unconditional, check whether Ishimoto also supplies (i) for the classes met in the cuspidality step of Lemma 6.10, or give an unconditional replacement for that step.

items.name: The global component group S_φ, the representations π_η and ε_φ
items.statement: Let φ = ⊕_i φ_i be a generic elliptic A-parameter for Mp_2n (pairwise distinct irreducible symplectic cuspidal φ_i of GL_{n_i}(A)). S_φ = ⊕_i (Z/2Z)a_i is the free Z/2Z-module with basis {a_i}, a_i ↔ φ_i. For each place v there is a canonical map S_φ → S_{φ_v}; S_{φ,A} = ∏_v S_{φ_v} is a compact group with diagonal map Δ : S_φ → S_{φ,A}, and Ŝ_{φ,A} = ⊕_v Ŝ_{φ_v} is its group of continuous characters. For η = ⊗_v η_v ∈ Ŝ_{φ,A} (η_v trivial and π_{η_v} unramified for almost all v), π_η = ⊗_v π_{η_v} with π_{η_v} ∈ Π_{φ_v,ψ_v}(Mp_2n) attached to η_v. ε_φ is the quadratic character of S_φ with ε_φ(a_i) = ε(1/2, φ_i) ∈ {±1}, the root number of φ_i.
items.note: The paper also remarks that π_η is expected to be tempered, by the Ramanujan conjecture for general linear groups. Review note: Missing and routed to route 1: correct. ML.4 plans Arthur's component groups for SO, not the Mp_2n version with ε_φ.

items.name: Rank of unitary representations; low rank
items.statement: Let F be a local field of characteristic zero, ψ a nontrivial character of F and V split, dim V = 2r + 1. Following Howe (1982) and J.-S. Li (Compositio Math. 71 (1989)): fix a maximal isotropic subspace X of V (dim X = r) with stabilizer P = MN in SO(V), and let Z be the centre of N. Z is identified with ∧²X, so through ψ its unitary characters are alternating forms on an r-dimensional space, and these have even rank. For an irreducible unitary representation σ of SO(V), σ|_Z defines a projection-valued measure on Ẑ, and σ has rank k if this measure is concentrated on the forms of rank k. Following [47, §4], σ is of low rank if its rank, which is necessarily even, is less than r − 1.
items.note: Howe, 'On a notion of rank for unitary representations of the classical groups' (1982); Li, 'On the classification of irreducible low rank unitary representations of classical groups', Compositio Math. 71 (1989). Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18): statement corrected against the paper: The item names 'rank' but does not define it. The paper defers to Howe [34] and Li [47] and gives no definition, but an item that serves as a definition needs one. The definition should be checked against [47, §§1–2, 4] (Compositio Math. 71), because the paper does not reproduce it. Review note: Missing is right; nothing in the atlas plans Howe–Li rank.

items.name: Local theta lifts in the stable range (J.-S. Li)
items.statement: Assume 2n < r − 1, so that (Mp_2n, SO_2r+1) is in the stable range (Li, Invent. Math. 97, Def. 5.1), and let F be local. For every π ∈ Irr Mp_2n the theta lift θ_ψ(π) to SO_2r+1 is nonzero, and if π is unitary so is θ_ψ(π) (Li, Invent. Math. 97). The map (π, χ) ↦ θ_ψ(π) ⊗ (χ ∘ ν) is a bijection (2.2) from {irreducible genuine unitary representations of Mp_2n} × {quadratic characters of F^×} onto {irreducible unitary representations of SO_2r+1 of rank 2n} (Li, Compositio Math. 71).
items.note: Review note: Statement matches p. 975. The paper does not attribute the nonvanishing to [48]: it is standard for the stable range, and only the unitarity is 'by [48]'. Missing, route 1: correct.

items.name: Global rank and theta lifts (Howe; J.-S. Li)
items.statement: Let F be a number field, 2n < r − 1, and σ = ⊗_v σ_v an irreducible unitary representation of SO_2r+1(A) occurring as a subrepresentation of A(SO_2r+1). The following are equivalent (Howe, LNM 880; Li, Amer. J. Math. 119, Lemma 3.2): σ is of rank 2n; σ_v is of rank 2n for all v; σ_v is of rank 2n for some v. In that case, for each v there are a unique irreducible genuine unitary π_v of Mp_2n(F_v) and a unique quadratic character χ_v of F_v^× with σ_v ≅ θ_{ψ_v}(π_v) ⊗ (χ_v ∘ ν); χ_v is unramified for almost all v and χ = ⊗_v χ_v is automorphic (Li, Amer. J. Math. 119, Prop. 5.7). Hence π_v is unramified for almost all v, and σ ≅ θ^abs_ψ(π) ⊗ (χ ∘ ν) for the abstract representation π = ⊗_v π_v of Mp_2n(A).
items.note: Review note: Statement matches pp. 975–976. Missing, route 1: correct.

items.name: Theorem 2.1 (J.-S. Li)
items.statement: Let F be a number field and assume 2n < r − 1. For an irreducible genuine unitary representation π of Mp_2n(A) with abstract theta lift θ^abs_ψ(π) to SO_2r+1(A): m_disc(π) ≤ m_disc(θ^abs_ψ(π)) ≤ m(θ^abs_ψ(π)) ≤ m(π).
items.note: J.-S. Li, 'Automorphic forms with degenerate Fourier coefficients', Amer. J. Math. 119 (1997). The paper's key tool: it lifts square-integrable, not necessarily cuspidal, representations of Mp_2n(A) to SO_2r+1(A), and back via Fourier–Jacobi coefficients. Review note: Matches Theorem 2.1 exactly (checked on the page image). Missing, route 1: correct.

items.name: The abstract theta lift
items.statement: Let F be a number field, ψ a nontrivial character of F\A, V a quadratic space over F as in §2.1 (dim V = 2r + 1, trivial discriminant), and π = ⊗_v π_v an abstract irreducible genuine representation of Mp_2n(A) such that the local theta lift θ_{ψ_v}(π_v) to SO(V)(F_v) (the lift to O(V)(F_v), restricted to SO(V)(F_v)) is nonzero for all v. Then θ_{ψ_v}(π_v) is irreducible for all v and unramified for almost all v, and θ^abs_ψ(π) = ⊗_v θ_{ψ_v}(π_v) is an abstract irreducible representation of SO(V)(A), the abstract theta lift of π. In the same way, when r ≥ n and σ = ⊗_v σ_v is an abstract irreducible representation of SO(V)(A) with θ_{ψ_v}(σ_v) ≠ 0 for all v (θ_{ψ_v}(σ_v) as in item conservation-relation), θ^abs_ψ(σ) = ⊗_v θ_{ψ_v}(σ_v) is its abstract theta lift to Mp_2n(A). The notation θ^abs_{V,Ψ} records the space V and the character Ψ (§6.3). The local stable-range correspondence is written ϑ_ψ in §6 (p. 991).
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18): statement corrected against the paper: The last sentence says 'ϑ^abs_ψ between Mp_2n(A) and SO_2r+1(A)' is defined in the same way. The paper has no ϑ^abs. ϑ_ψ is introduced in §6, p. 991, only as notation for the local theta correspondence of the stable-range pair (Mp_2n, SO_2r+1), to distinguish it from θ_ψ for the equal-rank pairs. The global abstract lifts used later are θ^abs_ψ(σ) from SO_2r+1(A) to Mp_2n(A) (proof of Proposition 4.4, p. 984), θ^abs_{V,Ψ}(Π) and θ^abs_Ψ(Σ) (§6.3, pp. 997–1000). Review note: Missing is right.

items.name: The global theta lift of a cuspidal representation
items.statement: Let F be a number field, ψ a nontrivial character of F\A and V as in §2.1. For an irreducible genuine cuspidal automorphic representation π ⊂ A_cusp(Mp_2n) of Mp_2n(A), the global theta lift Θ^aut_ψ(π) is the subspace of A(SO(V)) spanned by the automorphic forms θ(f, ϕ)(h) = ∫_{Sp_2n(F)\Mp_2n(A)} θ(f)(g, h) \overline{ϕ(g)} dg (complex conjugate of ϕ) for f ∈ ω_ψ and ϕ ∈ π. Here ω_ψ is the Weil representation of Mp_2n(A) × O(V)(A) and θ(f) is the (slowly increasing) theta function of f. The global theta lift of a cuspidal representation of SO(V)(A) to Mp_2n(A), and Θ^aut_{V,Ψ}(𝒱) for a realization 𝒱 ⊂ A_cusp(Mp_2n) of Π (proof of Lemma 6.8), are defined in the same way.
items.note: MP.5: 'Prove convergence of the theta lift where used.' Cusp forms decay rapidly, so these integrals converge. Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18): statement corrected against the paper: The integrand is missing its complex conjugation. p. 975 prints θ(f, ϕ)(h) = ∫_{Sp_2n(F)\Mp_2n(A)} θ(f)(g, h) \overline{ϕ(g)} dg, with a bar over ϕ(g); this was checked on the page image, and arXiv v3 p. 8 also has the bar (the text layer drops it). Without the bar, (f, ϕ) ↦ θ(f, ϕ) is an Mp_2n(A)-invariant pairing of ω_ψ with π, so Θ^aut would be a quotient of the π^∨-isotypic part of ω_ψ. The isomorphism Θ^aut_ψ(π) ≅ θ^abs_ψ(π) of item kudla-rallis-irreducibility would then be false in general, because it would hold with θ^abs_ψ(π^∨) instead. Review note: Planned in MP.5 ('Prove convergence of the theta lift where used') is right: cusp forms decay rapidly.

items.name: Irreducibility of square-integrable global theta lifts
items.statement: Let F be a number field, ψ a nontrivial character of F\A, V as in §2.1, and π an irreducible genuine cuspidal automorphic representation of Mp_2n(A), with Θ^aut_ψ(π) as in item automorphic-theta (with \overline{ϕ(g)}). If Θ^aut_ψ(π) is nonzero and contained in A²(SO(V)), then θ_{ψ_v}(π_v) ≠ 0 for all v, Θ^aut_ψ(π) is irreducible, and Θ^aut_ψ(π) ≅ θ^abs_ψ(π) (Kudla–Rallis, Ann. of Math. 140 (1994), Cor. 7.1.3).
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18): statement corrected against the paper: Minor. The hypotheses come only from context: π must be an irreducible genuine cuspidal automorphic representation of Mp_2n(A) (Θ^aut_ψ is defined only for such π), and Θ^aut_ψ(π) must be defined with the complex conjugate. The conclusion also implicitly contains θ_{ψ_v}(π_v) ≠ 0 for all v, which θ^abs_ψ(π) needs in order to be defined. Review note: Missing is right.

items.name: The tower property and cuspidality of global theta lifts
items.statement: Let Φ be a generic elliptic A-parameter for Mp_2n and V ⊂ A_cusp(Mp_2n) a realization of an irreducible summand Π of L²_{Φ,Ψ}(Mp_2n). For every (2n + 1)-dimensional quadratic space V over F with trivial discriminant, the global theta lift Θ^aut_{V,Ψ}(V) to SO(V)(A) is cuspidal (possibly zero). The same holds for global theta lifts from SO(V)(A) to Mp_2n(A) of cuspidal representations in L²_Φ(SO(V)).
items.locator: Proofs of Lemmas 6.8 and 6.10, pp. 996–998 (arXiv v3 pp. 25–26)
items.note: The paper deduces this 'from the tower property and the local theta correspondence for unramified representations' (Rallis): the earlier lifts in the Witt tower vanish because Φ is generic. Review note: 'Missing' and route 1 are right: no atlas stage mentions Rallis's tower property (searched 'Rallis', 'tower property', 'Witt tower'). The argument needs two inputs that should be stated. First, the unramified correspondence below the equal-rank range: a lift from Mp_2n to SO_{2n−1} forces |·|^{±1/2} into the Satake parameter of Π_v. Item unramified-theta covers only r ≥ n (see coverage). Second, the bound |Re s| < 1/2 on the Satake exponents of the cuspidal Φ_i (Jacquet–Shalika). The SO(V) → Mp_{2n−2} direction is covered by (3.2).

items.name: The Rallis inner product formula and its consequences
items.statement: Let F be a number field and Ψ a nontrivial character of F\A. (a) Let Π be an irreducible genuine cuspidal representation of Mp_2n(A) whose global theta lifts Θ^aut_{V,Ψ}(V) to the groups SO(V)(A) (dim V = 2n + 1, trivial discriminant) are cuspidal for every realization V of Π. If L^S_Ψ(1/2, Π) ≠ 0, then by the Rallis inner product formula (Kudla–Rallis, Ann. of Math. 140; Gan–Qiu–Takeda, Invent. Math. 198; Yamana, Invent. Math. 196) and the local Shimura correspondence there is a unique V such that Θ^aut_{V,Ψ}(V) ≠ 0 for every realization V of Π. (b) If the global theta lift of Π to the split SO_2n+1(A) is nonzero and cuspidal, then L_Ψ(1/2, Π) ≠ 0. (c) Let Φ be a generic elliptic A-parameter and Σ a cuspidal representation in L²_Φ(SO(V)). If L(1/2, Φ) ≠ 0, then the global theta lift Θ^aut_Ψ(Σ) to Mp_2n(A) is nonzero and cuspidal. (d) If Π is cuspidal, its global theta lift to SO_2r+1(A) in the stable range is nonzero and square-integrable.
items.locator: §1.4; proofs of Lemmas 6.8 and 6.10 and of Proposition A.1, pp. 971–1002 (arXiv v3 pp. 5–29)
items.note: (a) is in the proof of Lemma 6.8, (b) in the proof of Proposition A.1, (c) in the proof of Lemma 6.10, and (d) in §1.4, where it motivates J.-S. Li's method; (d) is not used in the proofs. The paper does not state the formula itself. Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18): statement corrected against the paper: Part (c) omits that Φ is a generic elliptic A-parameter, which gives cuspidality of the lift by the tower property so that the inner product formula applies. It also omits the conclusion that the lift is cuspidal: the proof of Lemma 6.10 (p. 998) says 'nonzero and cuspidal'. Review note: 'Missing' and route 1 are right; no stage plans the Rallis inner product formula or the regularized Siegel–Weil formula (searched). In (a) the existence of V is not given by the formula alone: it needs the spaces V_v attached to Π_v by the local Shimura correspondence to be coherent, ∏_v ε(V_v) = 1. This follows from Gan–Savin's ε-dichotomy and from ε(1/2, Φ) = 1, since L(1/2, Φ) ≠ 0. The paper cites [24] (Gan–Savin, 'epsilon dichotomy') for this, so it is not recorded as a mistake; it is proposed as a coverage item.

items.name: Multiplicity preservation (Gan)
items.statement: Let Φ be a generic elliptic A-parameter for Mp_2n and Π an irreducible genuine cuspidal summand of L²_{Φ,Ψ}(Mp_2n). Let V be a (2n + 1)-dimensional quadratic space with trivial discriminant such that Θ^aut_{V,Ψ}(V) is nonzero and cuspidal for every realization V of Π, and put Σ = θ^abs_{V,Ψ}(Π). Suppose the global theta lifts from SO(V)(A) to Mp_2n(A) of cuspidal realizations of Σ are nonzero and cuspidal; this holds here by the tower property and the Rallis inner product formula. Then m_cusp(Σ) = m_cusp(Π), so m_disc(Σ) ≥ m_cusp(Σ) = m_cusp(Π) (Gan, Progr. Math. 258, Prop. 2.6).
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 6.8, p. 997 (arXiv v3 p. 25)
items.note: Stated as used; the hypotheses of Gan's Proposition 2.6 were not read. Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18): statement corrected against the paper: The hypotheses name only the lifts from Mp_2n(A) to SO(V)(A). The equality m_cusp(Σ) = m_cusp(Π) also needs the lifts back from cuspidal realizations of Σ to Mp_2n(A) to be nonzero and cuspidal, so that the adjointness of the two theta maps gives injections both ways. In the proof of Lemma 6.8 these hold by the tower property (Φ generic) and the Rallis inner product formula. The exact hypotheses of Gan's Prop. 2.6 were not read, so check this against the source. Review note: 'Missing' and route 1 are right.

items.name: Nonvanishing and genericity of the lift of generic cusp forms (Furusawa)
items.statement: If Π is an irreducible genuine globally ψ-generic cuspidal automorphic representation of Mp_2n(A) whose global theta lift Σ = Θ^aut_ψ(Π) to the split SO_2n+1(A) is cuspidal, then Σ is nonzero and globally generic (Furusawa, J. reine angew. Math. 466 (1995)).
items.locator: Proof of Proposition A.1, p. 1002 (arXiv v3 p. 29)
items.note: Stated as used ('By [15], Σ is nonzero and globally generic'). Hence Σ is irreducible. Review note: missing; no stage plans Whittaker coefficients of theta lifts (MP.5 plans only Fourier–Whittaker expansions on the cover), so route 1 is right. The statement is as used on p. 1002; the cuspidality hypothesis is not needed for Furusawa's nonvanishing but is harmless. Ichino–Lapid–Mao (arXiv:1404.2909v2, App. A, before Prop. A.7) cite the same fact as [Fur95, Prop. 3], for the theta ψ^{-1}-lift of ψ_Ñ-generic forms. The item must pin the ψ/ψ^{-1} normalization of the generic character and of the Weil representation. The irreducibility of Σ that the note mentions follows from cuspidality and Howe duality (item kudla-rallis-irreducibility), not from genericity.

items.name: Supercuspidality of the local theta lift of a descent
items.statement: Let F_{v0} be a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero and π_{v0} an irreducible genuine ψ_{v0}-generic supercuspidal representation of Mp_2n(F_{v0}). Its theta lift θ_{ψ_{v0}}(π_{v0}) to the split SO_2n+1(F_{v0}) is nonzero, generic and square-integrable. It is supercuspidal (equivalently, π_{v0} has zero theta lift to the split SO_2n−1(F_{v0})) if and only if the L-parameter of π_{v0} relative to ψ_{v0} does not contain the summand S_2. In the other case θ_{ψ_{v0}}(π_{v0}) embeds in ν^{1/2} ⋊ σ′ with σ′ a generic supercuspidal representation of SO_2n−1(F_{v0}). For n = 1 the exceptional π_{v0} is exactly the odd Weil representation relative to ψ_{v0}, whose lift is the Steinberg representation. In particular, if π_{v0} is the descent relative to ψ_{v0} of an irreducible supercuspidal τ_{v0} of GL_2n(F_{v0}) such that L(s, τ_{v0}, ∧²) has a pole at s = 0, its parameter is irreducible and θ_{ψ_{v0}}(π_{v0}) is supercuspidal. Sources: Jiang–Soudry, Ann. of Math. 157 (2003), Th. 2.2(1); Kudla, Invent. Math. 83 (1986); Atobe–Gan, Invent. Math. 210 (2017), Th. 4.1; Bakić–Hanzer, arXiv:1902.07357, Prop. 3.5.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition A.1, p. 1002 (arXiv v3 p. 29)
items.note: Stated as used, so that the global theta lift in Proposition A.1 is cuspidal. Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18): statement corrected against the paper: The statement, for descents of supercuspidal τ_{v0}, is true, but it is not what [41, Th. 2.2] says. It is also narrower than what the proof of Proposition A.2 uses, since that proof needs it for an arbitrary π_{v0}. Jiang–Soudry, Th. 2.2 (Ann. of Math. 157, p. 767), read, says: (1) a generic supercuspidal σ of SO_2n+1 has a unique ψ-Howe lift to Mp_2n, which is supercuspidal and ψ-generic; (2) for n ≥ 2, the lift of every ψ-generic supercuspidal π of Mp_2n to SO_2n+1 is supercuspidal and generic. Part (2) is false for n ≥ 2 when the L-parameter of π contains S_2 (new issue below; Bakić–Hanzer, arXiv:1902.07357, Prop. 3.5(2)). For the descent of a supercuspidal τ_{v0} the parameter is irreducible, so the conclusion holds. It follows from Bakić–Hanzer Prop. 3.5(1), or from Th. 2.2(1) applied to the generic supercuspidal σ whose lift to GL_2n is τ_{v0}. Review note: missing; route 1 is right. The local first-occurrence half (Kudla) is plausibly within MP.3's 'explicitly needed first-occurrence/vanishing comparisons'. The parameter criterion needs Gan–Savin (item local-shimura) and Atobe–Gan.

items.name: The genuine discrete spectrum and multiplicities
items.statement: L²_disc(Mp_2n) is the discrete spectrum of the unitary representation L²(Mp_2n) of Mp_2n(A). For an irreducible genuine representation π of Mp_2n(A): m(π) = dim Hom_{Mp_2n(A)}(π, A(Mp_2n)), m_disc(π) = dim Hom(π, A²(Mp_2n)) and m_cusp(π) = dim Hom(π, A_cusp(Mp_2n)), so m_cusp(π) ≤ m_disc(π) ≤ m(π); likewise m(σ), m_disc(σ), m_cusp(σ) for representations σ of SO(V)(A).
items.note: AS.4 plans the discrete spectrum for linear groups; MP.8 warns that linear-group spectral results are not automatic for covers. Review note: Missing is right. AS.4 plans the spectral decomposition for linear groups only, and MP.8 says linear results do not transfer to covers automatically.

items.name: Near equivalence
items.statement: Two irreducible representations π = ⊗_v π_v and π′ = ⊗_v π′_v of Mp_2n(A) are nearly equivalent if π_v ≅ π′_v for almost all places v. A near equivalence class in L²_disc(Mp_2n) gives L-parameters ϕ_v : L_{F_v} → Sp_2n(C) for almost all v, such that for every irreducible summand π of the class the L-parameter of π_v relative to ψ_v is ϕ_v for almost all v.

items.name: Proposition 3.1 (the A-parameter of a near equivalence class)
items.statement: Let C be a near equivalence class contained in L²_disc(Mp_2n), with L-parameters ϕ_v. There is a unique elliptic A-parameter φ for Mp_2n with ϕ_{φ_v} = ϕ_v for almost all v.
items.note: Proof: fix r > 2n + 1 and π in C. Theorem 2.1 puts θ^abs_ψ(π) in L²_disc(SO_2r+1), which Arthur attaches to an elliptic A-parameter φ′. By (3.1) and (3.3), L^S(s, θ^abs_ψ(π)) = L^S_ψ(s, π) ∏_{j=1}^{2r−2n} ζ^S(s + r − n + 1/2 − j) is holomorphic for Re s > r − n + 1/2 with a pole there, which forces φ′ = φ ⊕ S_{2r−2n}. Uniqueness is strong multiplicity one. Review note: Missing, route 1: correct. Proof checked line by line. (i) The pole at s = r − n + 1/2 also needs L^S_ψ(r − n + 1/2, π) ≠ 0, which the paper does not state (new issue below). (ii) The step 'if t is the largest such integer, then L^S(s, θ^abs_ψ(π)) has a pole at s = t + 1/2' holds by a dimension count the paper leaves implicit. Since r > 2n + 1, 2t ≥ 2r − 2n > r, so every other block of φ′ has n_k d_k ≤ 2r − 2t ≤ 2n < 2t, and at s = t + 1/2 all other factors of (3.1) are evaluated at arguments with real part ≥ t + 1 − n > 1, where they are finite and nonzero. (iii) Uniqueness uses item strong-multiplicity-one: the multiset of centred strings {(φ_i, d_i)} is recovered from the isobaric sum ⊞ φ_i|·|^{(d_i+1)/2−j}.

items.name: Theorem 1.1 (decomposition into near equivalence classes)
items.statement: Let F be a number field and fix a nontrivial additive character ψ of F\A.
