Then L²_disc(Mp_2n) = ⊕_φ L²_{φ,ψ}(Mp_2n), where the sum runs over elliptic A-parameters φ for Mp_2n and L²_{φ,ψ}(Mp_2n) is a full near equivalence class of irreducible representations π in L²_disc(Mp_2n) such that the L-parameter of π_v (relative to ψ_v) is ϕ_{φ_v} for almost all places v of F.
items.locator: §1.1, Theorem 1.1; proved in §3.2, pp. 967–978 (arXiv v3 pp. 3–11)
items.note: Unconditional. L²_{φ,ψ}(Mp_2n) may be zero for some φ. Review note: Missing, route 1: correct. The paper leaves one step implicit: distinct near equivalence classes receive distinct φ, because at almost all v an unramified genuine π_v is determined by its ψ_v-relative parameter (the unique unramified subquotient of (5.5); item rmk-5-3).

items.name: Remark 1.2 (no embedded eigenvalues)
items.statement: Mp_2n has no embedded eigenvalues: every family of eigenvalues of the unramified Hecke algebras on the automorphic discrete spectrum of Mp_2n is distinct from those on the automorphic continuous spectrum of Mp_2n.
items.note: The paper says it 'immediately follows from Theorem 1.1'; this is the analogue of Arthur's result for classical groups (Clay Math. Proc. 13), which Arthur needed as an input, whereas here it is deduced from the classification. Review note: Missing, route 1: correct. 'Immediately' hides inputs that no item covers: Langlands' spectral decomposition of L²(Mp_2n), with its continuous spectrum from Eisenstein series on Levi covers (coverage row), Theorem 1.1 for Mp_2m with m < n, Mœglin–Waldspurger's residual spectrum of GL_k, and strong multiplicity one. The deduction checks out. An Eisenstein family at λ ∈ i a*_M contains τ|·|^λ and τ^∨|·|^{−λ}; matching ⊞ φ_i|·|^{(d_i+1)/2−j} forces them to be self-dual and so repeats some (φ_i, d_i), because a multiset of centred strings decomposes uniquely into strings. (1.1) excludes that repetition.

items.name: Remark 1.3 (dependence on ψ)
items.statement: Let ψ_a(x) = ψ(ax) with a ∈ F^×. For φ = ⊕_i φ_i ⊠ S_{d_i} put φ_a = ⊕_i (φ_i ⊗ (χ_a ∘ det)) ⊠ S_{d_i}, where χ_a is the quadratic character of A^× attached to F(√a)/F. For every irreducible summand π of L²_{φ,ψ_a}(Mp_2n) the L-parameter of π_v relative to ψ_v is ϕ_{φ_{a,v}} for almost all v; hence L²_{φ,ψ_a}(Mp_2n) = L²_{φ_a,ψ}(Mp_2n).
items.note: Stated without proof; it follows from the dependence of the unramified correspondence on ψ. Review note: Missing, route 1: correct. Checked: at the places where a is a unit, χ_{ψ_a}(x) = χ_ψ(x)(a, x), so the ψ_v-parameter of π_v is its ψ_{a,v}-parameter twisted by χ_{a,v} (Gan–Savin, Th. 12.1, item llc-mp). φ_a is again elliptic, since L(s, φ_i ⊗ χ_a, ∧²) = L(s, φ_i, ∧²) because χ_a² = 1.

items.name: Remark 3.2 (embedding into L²_φ′(SO_2r+1))
items.statement: Suppose L²_{φ,ψ}(Mp_2n) ≅ ⊕_π m_π π, the sum over irreducible genuine representations π of Mp_2n(A) with m_π the multiplicity of π in L²_{φ,ψ}(Mp_2n). If r > 2n + 1 and φ′ = φ ⊕ S_{2r−2n}, then ⊕_π m_π θ^abs_ψ(π) embeds in L²_φ′(SO_2r+1).
items.note: From Theorem 2.1 and Howe duality. Corollary 4.2 shows the embedding is an isomorphism when φ is generic. Review note: Missing, route 1: correct. Checked: it uses unitarity of the summands π (needed for Theorem 2.1), the identification in the proof of Proposition 3.1 of the A-parameter of θ^abs_ψ(π) as φ ⊕ S_{2r−2n}, and injectivity of θ on isomorphism classes at every place (Howe duality).

items.name: Remark 3.3 (multiplicity one over totally imaginary fields)
items.statement: By Arthur's multiplicity formula (Th. 1.5.2), once local A-packets are known to be multiplicity-free, m_disc(σ) ≤ 1 for every irreducible representation σ of SO_2r+1(A). Local A-packets are multiplicity-free for F nonarchimedean (Mœglin) and F = C (Mœglin; Mœglin–Renard). Hence, by Theorem 2.1, L²_disc(Mp_2n) is multiplicity-free when F is totally imaginary.
items.note: The real case was not fully known (Arancibia–Mœglin–Renard, Mœglin–Renard). This gives multiplicity one for the whole discrete spectrum over totally imaginary fields, including the non-generic part. Review note: Missing, route 1: correct. Checked: with r > 2n + 1 and no real places, m_disc(π) ≤ m_disc(θ^abs_ψ(π)) ≤ 1. It also uses that distinct elliptic φ′ give disjoint near equivalence classes (strong multiplicity one).

items.name: Non-cuspidal automorphic representations embed in induced representations
items.statement: Let V ⊂ A(Mp_2n) realize an irreducible genuine π with V ⊄ A_cusp(Mp_2n), and let P = MN be a proper parabolic subgroup of Sp_2n, minimal such that the image V_P of V under the constant term map A(Mp_2n) → A_P(Mp_2n) is nonzero. Then V_P consists of cusp forms and π is a subrepresentation of Ind_{P̃(A)}^{Mp_2n(A)}(ρ) for an irreducible cuspidal automorphic representation ρ of M̃(A). Here A_P(Mp_2n) is the space of genuine automorphic forms on N(A)M(F)\Mp_2n(A).
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 4.1, pp. 979–980 (arXiv v3 p. 12)
items.note: The paper cites '[44, p. 205]' for linear groups; the published reference list gives the wrong paper for [44] (sourceIssues E4). The argument is Langlands' in 'On the notion of an automorphic representation', for reductive groups; the paper applies it to the cover without comment. AF.3 plans constant terms and cusp forms for linear groups and MP.5 constant terms on the cover. Review note: 'Missing' is confirmed. AF.3 plans constant terms and cusp forms for linear groups, and MP.5 constant terms on the cover. AS.1 and AS.4 treat cuspidal data only inside the spectral decomposition. No stage plans Langlands' theorem that an automorphic representation embeds in, or is a constituent of, a representation induced from a cuspidal one. Its source is Langlands, 'On the notion of an automorphic representation', PSPM 33, Part 1, pp. 203–207, which I read (IAS copy). The argument cited as [44, p. 205] is there: the projection of the constant term along a minimal parabolic onto an irreducible cuspidal component H realizes π as a quotient of V′ ⊂ Ind δ^{−1}σ. For irreducible V this is an embedding. E4 is confirmed.

items.name: Proposition 4.1 (the key equality)
items.statement: Let φ be a generic elliptic A-parameter for Mp_2n and π an irreducible genuine representation of Mp_2n(A) such that the L-parameter of π_v (relative to ψ_v) is φ_v for almost all v. Then m_cusp(π) = m_disc(π) = m(π).
items.note: Proof: if a realization were not cuspidal, π ↪ Ind(ρ) with ρ ≅ (⊗_i τ̃_{i,ψ}) ⊗ π_0; by Proposition 3.1, π_0 has a weak lift τ_0, so π has the weak lift ⊞_i (τ_i ⊞ τ_i^∨) ⊞ τ_0 (4.1) as well as ⊞_i φ_i (4.2). Strong multiplicity one then gives a contradiction: each τ_i is non-self-dual or occurs at least twice, while the φ_i are self-dual and occur once.

items.name: Corollary 4.2 (multiplicity preservation)
items.statement: Let φ be a generic elliptic A-parameter for Mp_2n with L²_{φ,ψ}(Mp_2n) ≅ ⊕_π m_π π. If r > 2n + 1 and φ′ = φ ⊕ S_{2r−2n}, then L²_φ′(SO_2r+1) ≅ ⊕_π m_π θ^abs_ψ(π).
items.note: Proof: m_disc(π) = m_disc(θ^abs_ψ(π)) (4.3), by Theorem 2.1 and Proposition 4.1. Every σ in L²_φ′(SO_2r+1) is locally θ_ψ(π_{φ_v}) for almost all v (4.4), so it has rank 2n and σ ≅ θ^abs_ψ(π) ⊗ (χ ∘ ν). Comparing with the bijection (2.2) shows χ_v is trivial for almost all v, so χ = 1.

items.name: Lemma 4.3 (the sign character)
items.statement: Let φ = ⊕_i φ_i be a generic elliptic A-parameter for Mp_2n, φ′ = φ ⊕ S_{2r−2n} with r > 2n + 1, S_φ′ = S_φ ⊕ (Z/2Z)a′_0, and ι : S_φ ↪ S_φ′ ↠ S̄_φ′ the natural isomorphism; put ε_φ = ι*ε_φ′. Then ε_φ(a_i) = ε(1/2, φ_i). Moreover, if L(1/2, φ) ≠ 0 then ε_φ is trivial.
items.note: Proof: in the decomposition Ad ∘ φ̃′ = (Ad ∘ φ̃) ⊕ (φ̃ ⊠ S_{2r−2n}) ⊕ S_3 ⊕ S_7 ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ S_{4r−4n−1}, only φ̃ ⊠ S_{2r−2n} = ⊕_i κ_i κ′_0 ⊠ Std_i ⊠ S_{2r−2n} contributes to Arthur's ε_φ′. If L(1/2, φ) = ∏_i L(1/2, φ_i) ≠ 0 then every ε(1/2, φ_i) = 1. The decomposition of Sym² S_{2r−2n} was checked. Review note: 'Missing' is correct. Comment on the proof, not an issue. The paper justifies 'Ad ∘ φ̃ does not contribute' by 'Ad ∘ φ̃ is orthogonal'. On its own that is not enough, since an orthogonal representation can contain symplectic irreducibles, for example ρ ⊕ ρ with ρ symplectic. The step is nevertheless right: Ad ∘ φ̃ = ⊕_i Sym² Std_i ⊕ ⊕_{i<j} Std_i ⊠ Std_j, and each of these summands is irreducible and orthogonal as a representation of L_φ = ∏ Sp_{n_i}(C). The note should record this.

items.name: The representations π̃_η transported from SO_2r+1
items.statement: Let φ be a generic elliptic A-parameter for Mp_2n, φ′ = φ ⊕ S_{2r−2n} with r > 2n + 1, and ι_v : S_{φ_v} ↪ S_{φ′_v} ↠ S̄_{φ′_v} the natural isomorphism. For η′_v ∈ (S̄_{φ′_v})^ write σ_{η′_v} = ⊕_i m_{η′_v,i} σ_{η′_v,i} with pairwise distinct irreducible σ_{η′_v,i}, put η_v = ι*_v η′_v and π̃_{η_v} = ⊕_i m_{η′_v,i} θ_{ψ_v}(σ_{η′_v,i}), the theta lifts to Mp_2n(F_v). For η = ⊗_v η_v ∈ Ŝ_{φ,A}, π̃_η = ⊗_v π̃_{η_v} is a semisimple genuine representation of Mp_2n(A).
items.locator: §4.4, pp. 983–984 (ι_v is defined at the foot of p. 983, π̃_{η_v} and π̃_η on p. 984) (arXiv v3 p. 15)

items.name: Proposition 4.4 (the multiplicity formula with transported packets)
items.statement: Let φ be a generic elliptic A-parameter for Mp_2n. Then L²_{φ,ψ}(Mp_2n) ≅ ⊕_{η ∈ Ŝ_{φ,A}} m_η π̃_η, with m_η = 1 if Δ*η = ε_φ and 0 otherwise.
items.note: From Corollary 4.2, Howe duality and (4.5). Remark 4.5: π̃_η is not known a priori to be independent of r; this follows once π̃_η is described by the local Shimura correspondence (Proposition 6.1), a local statement the paper proves by a global argument.

items.name: Theorem 1.4 (the multiplicity formula for Mp_2n)
items.statement: Let F be a number field and φ a generic elliptic A-parameter for Mp_2n. Then L²_{φ,ψ}(Mp_2n) ≅ ⊕_{η ∈ Ŝ_{φ,A}} m_η π_η, where m_η = 1 if Δ*η = ε_φ and m_η = 0 otherwise. The paper proves this under the hypothesis that Arthur's result extends to non-split odd special orthogonal groups, in the form of the multiplicity formula (6.1); Ishimoto (IMRN 2024) has since proved (6.1) for generic parameters.
items.locator: §1.3, Theorem 1.4, p. 970 (arXiv v3 p. 5); proved in §4.4 (Proposition 4.4, p. 984) and §6 (Proposition 6.1, pp. 990–1001), with Propositions 6.5 and 6.6 proved in Appendix A (pp. 1001–1008) (arXiv v3 pp. 5–35)
items.note: Remark 1.5: the description is formally that of SO_2n+1, except that Δ*η = ε_φ replaces Δ*η = 1. For n = 1 the argument reproves the Shimura–Waldspurger correspondence for Mp_2 without Waldspurger's nonvanishing theorem for twisted central L-values. Review note: The proof uses Appendix A, which the old range pp. 970–1001 leaves out; hence the locator fix. 'Missing' is correct; route 1.

items.name: Corollary 1.6 (multiplicity one for the generic part)
items.statement: The generic part of L²_disc(Mp_2n), defined as ⊕_φ L²_{φ,ψ}(Mp_2n) over generic elliptic A-parameters φ, is multiplicity-free.
items.note: An immediate consequence of Theorems 1.1 and 1.4, so subject to the same hypothesis as Theorem 1.4 (removed by Ishimoto). It generalizes Waldspurger's result for Mp_2 (J. Math. Pures Appl. 59 (1980), p. 131).

items.name: Proposition 6.1 (comparison of local theta lifts)
items.statement: Let F be a local field of characteristic zero, ψ a nontrivial additive character, φ a 2n-dimensional almost tempered symplectic representation of L_F, φ′ = φ ⊕ S_{2r−2n} with r > 2n + 1 and ι : S_φ ↪ S_φ′ ↠ S̄_φ′ the natural isomorphism. For every η′ ∈ (S̄_φ′)^, ϑ_ψ(σ_η′) = π_η with η = ι*η′, where ϑ_ψ is the theta lift from SO_2r+1 to Mp_2n (the stable-range pair) and π_η ∈ Π_{φ,ψ}(Mp_2n) is defined through the local Shimura correspondence.
items.note: With Proposition 5.4 this is what the global argument needs: π̃_η = π_η in Proposition 4.4. The proof is by induction on n (Lemmas 6.2–6.4) and a global argument for good parameters (Lemmas 6.8–6.12), which uses (6.1) for possibly non-split SO(V). Review note: 'Missing' and route 1 are right. The statement presupposes Proposition 5.4 (σ_η′ nonzero and irreducible), which is proved at the same time. I checked the route to Theorem 1.4. Proposition 4.4 gives L²_{φ,ψ} ≅ ⊕ m_η π̃_η. Propositions 5.4 and 6.1 at every place (φ_v is almost tempered) give π̃_{η_v} = θ_{ψ_v}(σ_{η′_v}) = π_{η_v}. By Lemma 4.3, ε_φ = ι*ε_φ′ is the ε_φ of Theorem 1.4. Theorem 1.4 follows for every r > 2n + 1, which also settles Remark 4.5. The induction on n has to run over all local fields at once, because the good case over F uses Lemmas 6.3 and 6.4 at the other places of a number field, and the paper is arranged that way. Hypothesis (6.1) enters only through Lemmas 6.8–6.12 (good φ, F nonarchimedean or real). So Proposition 6.1 is unconditional only for F = C and for φ with no symplectic summand (Lemmas 6.2 and 6.3 with n_0 = 0). E2 (rejected) does not affect it.

items.name: Lemma 6.2 (n = 0)
items.statement: Propositions 5.4 and 6.1 hold for n = 0: φ′ = S_2r, Π_φ′(SO_2r+1) = {σ_1} with σ_1 trivial, and ϑ_ψ(σ_1) is the genuine 1-dimensional representation of Mp_0 = {±1}, which is also the theta lift of the trivial representation of SO_1 = {1}.

items.name: Lemma 6.3 (reduction to good parameters)
items.statement: If Propositions 5.4 and 6.1 hold for all 2n_0-dimensional good symplectic representations of L_F for all n_0 < n, then they hold for all 2n-dimensional almost tempered non-good symplectic representations of L_F.
items.note: Proof: σ_η′ is the semisimplification of Ind_Q′(τ ⊗ σ_{η′_0}), irreducible by Lemma 5.5; the induction principle gives a nonzero map ω_ψ → Ind_P̃(τ̃_ψ ⊗ π_{η_0}) ⊗ Ind_Q′(τ ⊗ σ_{η′_0}), and Lemma 5.2 makes the first factor irreducible. Multiplicity-freeness transfers from Π_{φ,ψ}(Mp_2n). After this lemma the proof is complete for F = C, where no parameter is good. Review note: I checked the proof on p. 992. E2 is rejected (see issues). The induction hypothesis applies to φ′_0 = φ_0 ⊕ S_{2r−2n} on SO_{2(r−k)+1} because 2r − 2n = 2(r − k) − 2n_0 and r − k > 2n_0 + 1 follows from r > 2n + 1. The identifications S_φ = S_{φ_0} and S̄_φ′ = S̄_{φ′_0} are compatible with ι. The ϑ_ψ(σ_η′) = π_η step also uses that π_η is a subquotient of Ind(τ̃_ψ ⊗ π_{η_0}), the inductive property in §5.3 (item llc-mp).

items.name: Lemma 6.4 (the trivial character)
items.statement: Let F be nonarchimedean or F = C and φ almost tempered. Let ϕ_φ′ be the L-parameter attached to φ′ by (5.6) and σ′ the member of the L-packet Π_{ϕ_φ′}(SO_2r+1) attached to the trivial character of S_{ϕ_φ′}. Then ϑ_ψ(σ′) = π_1, the member of Π_{φ,ψ}(Mp_2n) attached to the trivial character of S_φ.
items.note: For non-good φ: Arthur's Prop. 7.4.1 and Propositions 5.4 and 6.1 (known by Lemma 6.3). For good φ (so F nonarchimedean): σ′ is the Langlands quotient of Ind_Q′(|·|^{r−n−1/2} ⊗ |·|^{r−n−3/2} ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ |·|^{1/2} ⊗ σ), Q′ with Levi (GL_1)^{r−n} × SO_2n+1, σ ∈ Π_φ(SO_2n+1) attached to the trivial character; θ_ψ(σ) = π_1 on Mp_2n, and Gan–Takeda, Contemp. Math. 664, Prop. 3.2, gives ϑ_ψ(σ′) = π_1 (item gan-takeda-standard-module). Review note: Checked. The non-good case sits inside the induction: it uses Propositions 5.4 and 6.1 for φ, from Lemma 6.3. The good case uses Gan–Takeda Prop. 3.2, which I read in arXiv:1405.2626v3, p. 8 (see gan-takeda-standard-module).

items.name: Theta lifts of Langlands quotients (Gan–Takeda)
items.statement: Let F be a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero, ψ a nontrivial additive character and π ∈ Irr Mp_2n. Suppose θ_ψ(π) = σ is an irreducible tempered representation of the split SO_2n+1. Then for every r ≥ n the theta lift of π to the split SO_2r+1 (same Witt tower) is the unique irreducible quotient σ′ of the standard module Ind_{Q′}^{SO_2r+1}(|·|^{r−n−1/2} ⊗ |·|^{r−n−3/2} ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ |·|^{1/2} ⊗ σ), where Q′ has Levi component (GL_1)^{r−n} × SO_2n+1. Equivalently, by Howe duality, the theta lift of σ′ to Mp_2n is π. (Gan–Takeda, Contemp. Math. 664, Prop. 3.2, with d = 2n + 1, d′ = 2r + 1 and χ_W trivial.)
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 6.4, p. 992 (arXiv v3 p. 22)
items.note: Stated as used. Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18): statement corrected against the paper: The range of r and the Witt tower are not stated. Gan–Takeda Prop. 3.2 (arXiv:1405.2626v3, p. 8) takes V_{d′} = V_d ⊕ H^r with d ≥ n + ε_0, σ ⊂ θ_{W,V_d}(π) and σ′ ⊂ θ_{W,V_{d′}}(π). Here d = 2n + 1, because W has dimension 2n and ε_0 = 1. For tempered σ the conclusion holds for all r ≥ 0; the induced representation is then a standard module and σ′ is its Langlands quotient. The paper's form (the theta lift of σ′ to Mp_2n is π) follows by Howe duality. Review note: 'Missing' and route 1 are right.

items.name: Lemma 6.8 (multiplicity one in the A-packet)
items.statement: Let F be nonarchimedean or F = R, φ a 2n-dimensional good symplectic representation of L_F and φ′ = φ ⊕ S_{2r−2n} with r > 2n + 1. For an irreducible representation σ′ of SO_2r+1 and η′ ∈ (S̄_φ′)^ put m(σ′, η′) = dim Hom_{SO_2r+1}(σ′, σ_η′). Then m(σ′, η′) ≤ 1, with equality for at most one η′; that is, Π_φ′(SO_2r+1) is multiplicity-free.
items.note: Known from Mœglin for F nonarchimedean, but not fully for F = R. Proof: globalize with Corollary 6.7(i) at two places v_0, v_1; Arthur's formula (4.5) gives m_disc(Σ′) ≥ Σ_η′ m(σ′, η′)² > 0; lift to Mp_2n (Proposition 4.1, Corollary 4.2) and on to the unique SO(V) (Rallis inner product formula, multiplicity preservation); (6.1) gives m_disc(Σ) = 1. So 1 ≥ Σ_η′ m(σ′, η′)². V may be non-split, so the proof uses the hypothesis (6.1). Review note: I checked the whole proof. It uses (6.1) for a possibly non-split SO(V) (m_disc(Σ) = 1), the Rallis inner product formula together with the coherence of the local spaces, multiplicity preservation, and the fact that the theta correspondence depends only on the square class of ψ (for Ψ_{v0}, Ψ_{v1}). The last two inputs, and the existence of the number field F with F_{v0} ≅ F_{v1} ≅ F, are used without statement; see coverage.

items.name: Lemma 6.9 (injectivity)
items.statement: Let JH(Π_φ′(SO_2r+1)) be the set of equivalence classes of irreducible σ′ with m(σ′, η′) > 0 for some η′. The theta lift induces an injection ϑ_ψ : JH(Π_φ′(SO_2r+1)) ↪ Π_{φ,ψ}(Mp_2n).
items.note: The hypotheses are those of §6.3 (φ good, F nonarchimedean or R). Review note: Checked. The L-parameter of Σ_{v0} is φ because (6.1) puts every local component of a summand of L²_Φ(SO(V)) in Π_{Φ_v}(SO(V_v)). So Lemma 6.9 also depends on (6.1).

items.name: Lemma 6.10 (bijectivity)
items.statement: The theta lift induces a bijection ϑ_ψ : JH(Π_φ′(SO_2r+1)) ↔ Π_{φ,ψ}(Mp_2n).
items.note: Surjectivity: for η′, globalize Σ_η on SO(V) at v_0, v_1 (the global V exists by the product formula), lift Σ to Mp_2n (nonzero and cuspidal because L(1/2, Φ) ≠ 0) and then to SO_2r+1 by Corollary 4.2. Uses (6.1). Review note: Checked. Add to the note that Σ is proved cuspidal by 'the argument in the proof of Proposition 4.1'. That step needs weak lifts to GL of cuspidal representations on Levi subgroups of the possibly non-split SO(V), which is part (i) of the hypothesis (see amf-nonsplit).

items.name: Lemma 6.11 (irreducible good parameters)
items.statement: If φ is irreducible (and good), Propositions 5.4 and 6.1 hold for φ.
items.note: Proof: #JH(Π_φ′(SO_2r+1)) = 2. If σ′_1 (the trivial character) were reducible, a global representation with components σ′ and σ′′ at v_0 and v_1 would force ε(V_{v_0})ε(V_{v_1}) = −1 while ε(V_v) = 1 elsewhere (Lemma 6.4), contradicting ∏_v ε(V_v) = 1. The same argument over Q (Proposition 6.6) settles the real case, where n = 1. Review note: Checked, including the real case: F = Q, the only real place is v0 = ∞, and ε(V_∞) = η(z_φ) follows from the inclusion Ŝ_{φ,V} ⊂ {η(z_φ) = ε(V)}. The contradiction ∏_v ε(V_v) = −1 is correct in both cases.

items.name: Lemma 6.12 (reducible good parameters)
items.statement: If φ is reducible (and good), Propositions 5.4 and 6.1 hold for φ.
items.note: Proof: globalize with Corollary 6.7(ii) so that Φ_v is non-good for v ≠ v_0; choose ⊗_v ξ_v with ξ_{v_0} = η and (⊗_v ξ_v) ∘ Δ = 1 (6.2)–(6.3); (6.1) makes Σ = ⊗_v Σ_{ξ_v} automorphic; lifting twice and comparing (6.4), (6.5) gives ξ′_{v_0} = η′ (6.6). Review note: The proof ends on p. 1001 at (6.6) and 'This completes the proof'. I checked (6.2)–(6.6). 'By Lemma 6.8, such ξ′_v is unique' holds at v0. At v ≠ v0 the uniqueness comes from Proposition 5.4 for the non-good Φ_v, which the next sentence supplies.

items.name: Proposition 6.5 (globalizing symplectic parameters)
items.statement: Let F be a number field, S a nonempty finite set of nonarchimedean places and v_0 ∉ S a nonarchimedean place. For each v ∈ S let φ_v be a 2n-dimensional irreducible symplectic representation of L_{F_v}. Then there is an irreducible symplectic cuspidal automorphic representation Φ of GL_2n(A) such that Φ_v = φ_v for all v ∈ S; Φ_v is a sum of 1-dimensional representations for all nonarchimedean v ∉ S ∪ {v_0}; and L(1/2, Φ) ≠ 0 (Φ_v regarded as a representation of L_{F_v} through the local Langlands correspondence).
items.locator: §6.2, Proposition 6.5; proved in Appendix A.1, pp. 993–1005 (arXiv v3 pp. 23–32)
items.note: A refinement of the globalizations of Sakellaridis–Venkatesh (Astérisque 396, Th. 16.3.2) and Ichino–Lapid–Mao (Duke Math. J. 166, Cor. A.8). It follows from Proposition A.1, taking τ_{v_0} supercuspidal with symplectic parameter. Review note: I checked the statement on p. 993 and its deduction from Proposition A.1 (p. 1001). The deduction also needs a supercuspidal τ_{v0} with symplectic parameter (item symplectic-supercuspidal-existence).

items.name: Proposition 6.6 (globalizing 2-dimensional parameters)
items.statement: Let F be totally real, S a finite set of places containing all archimedean places and v_0 ∉ S a nonarchimedean place. For each v ∈ S let φ_v be a 2-dimensional irreducible symplectic representation of L_{F_v}. Then there is an irreducible symplectic cuspidal automorphic representation Φ of GL_2(A) such that Φ_v = φ_v for all v ∈ S; Φ_v is a sum of 1-dimensional representations for all v ∉ S ∪ {v_0}; and L(1/2, Φ) ≠ 0.
items.locator: §6.2, Proposition 6.6; proved in Appendix A.2, pp. 994–1008 (arXiv v3 pp. 23–35)
items.note: Every irreducible symplectic representation of L_R is 2-dimensional. It follows from Proposition A.3.

items.name: Corollary 6.7 (global parameters for the local argument)
items.statement: Let F be a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero or F = R, and φ a 2n-dimensional good symplectic representation of L_F. (i) Let F be a totally imaginary number field (resp. a real quadratic field) if F is nonarchimedean (resp. F = R), with two distinct places v_0, v_1 such that F_{v_0} = F_{v_1} = F. There is a generic elliptic A-parameter Φ for Mp_2n with Φ_{v_0} = Φ_{v_1} = φ, such that the natural maps S_Φ → S_{Φ_{v_0}} and S_Φ → S_{Φ_{v_1}} agree, and L(1/2, Φ) ≠ 0. (ii) Assume φ is reducible, and let F be a totally imaginary number field (resp. F = Q) if F is nonarchimedean (resp. F = R), with a place v_0 such that F_{v_0} = F. There is a generic elliptic A-parameter Φ for Mp_2n with Φ_{v_0} = φ, Φ_v non-good for all v ≠ v_0, S_Φ → S_{Φ_{v_0}} surjective, S_Φ → ∏_{v≠v_0} S_{Φ_v} injective, and L(1/2, Φ) ≠ 0.
items.note: Proof: globalize each irreducible summand φ_i separately with Propositions 6.5 and 6.6, using auxiliary places S_i = {v_i, v′_i} where Φ_{i,v_i} is irreducible; this uses the existence of 2n_i-dimensional irreducible symplectic representations of L_{F_v} at every nonarchimedean v (item symplectic-supercuspidal-existence). Review note: I checked the proof. At the auxiliary place v′_i of Proposition 6.5 or 6.6, Φ_{i,v′_i} is uncontrolled. For reducible φ, however, Φ_{j,v′_i} with j ≠ i is a sum of characters, so Φ_{v′_i} is still non-good, and the map S_Φ → ∏_i S_{Φ_{v_i}} is bijective as claimed. The number field F is an input of the corollary; its existence is a separate step (see coverage).

items.name: Existence of irreducible symplectic parameters
items.statement: For every nonarchimedean local field F_v of characteristic zero and every m ≥ 1 there is a 2m-dimensional irreducible symplectic representation of L_{F_v} (see Savin, J. Algebra 319 (2008), §2).
items.locator: Proof of Corollary 6.7, p. 995 (arXiv v3 p. 24); also used without statement in deducing Proposition 6.5 from Proposition A.1 (p. 1001), which needs a supercuspidal τ_{v0} with symplectic parameter
items.note: Review note: 'Missing' and route 1 are right; no stage plans it. The construction is standard: induce to W_{F_v} a regular conjugate-symplectic character of the unramified extension of degree 2m, as in Savin §2. It works in every residual characteristic.

items.name: Proposition A.1 (globalizing square-integrable representations of GL_2n)
items.statement: Let F be a number field, S a nonempty finite set of nonarchimedean places and v_0 ∉ S nonarchimedean. For each v ∈ S ∪ {v_0} let τ_v be an irreducible square-integrable representation of GL_2n(F_v) such that L(s, τ_v, ∧²) has a pole at s = 0, with τ_{v_0} supercuspidal. Then there is an irreducible cuspidal automorphic representation T of GL_2n(A) such that T_v = τ_v for all v ∈ S ∪ {v_0}; T_v is a principal series representation for all v ∉ S_∞ ∪ S ∪ {v_0}; L(s, T, ∧²) has a pole at s = 1; and L(1/2, T) ≠ 0.
items.locator: Appendix A.1, Proposition A.1 (p. 1001) and its proof (p. 1002; the proof ends on p. 1002), arXiv v3 pp. 29–30
items.note: Proof: descend τ_v to ψ_v-generic square-integrable π_v of Mp_2n(F_v); globalize with Proposition A.2; lift Π to the split SO_2n+1(A) (cuspidal because θ(π_{v_0}) is supercuspidal; nonzero and generic by Furusawa); the Rallis inner product formula gives L_ψ(1/2, Π) ≠ 0; take T the functorial lift of Σ to GL_2n(A); Ichino–Lapid–Mao, Prop. 4.3, gives T_v = τ_v. Review note: missing; no stage plans it; route 1 is right. The statement matches p. 1001. The proof is unaffected by the new issue below: the descents π_v it feeds into Proposition A.2 satisfy the corrected hypothesis (θ_{ψ_{v0}}(π_{v0}) supercuspidal). Deducing Proposition 6.5 also needs a supercuspidal τ_{v0} with an ∧²-pole (item symplectic-supercuspidal-existence).

items.name: Proposition A.2 (globalizing generic square-integrable representations of Mp_2n)
items.statement: Let F be a number field and ψ a nontrivial character of F\A, with the generic character of N(F)\N(A) that it defines (Gan–Gross–Prasad, Astérisque 346, §12). Let S be a nonempty finite set of nonarchimedean places and v_0 ∉ S a nonarchimedean place. For each v ∈ S ∪ {v_0} let π_v be an irreducible genuine ψ_v-generic square-integrable representation of Mp_2n(F_v). Assume that π_{v_0} is supercuspidal and that its theta lift θ_{ψ_{v_0}}(π_{v_0}) to the split SO_2n+1(F_{v_0}) is supercuspidal. Equivalently, the L-parameter of π_{v_0} relative to ψ_{v_0} does not contain S_2; for n = 1 this says exactly that π_{v_0} is not the odd Weil representation relative to ψ_{v_0}. Then there is an irreducible genuine globally ψ-generic cuspidal automorphic representation Π of Mp_2n(A) such that Π_v ≅ π_v for all v ∈ S ∪ {v_0}, and Π_v is an irreducible principal series representation for all v ∉ S_∞ ∪ S ∪ {v_0}. (The printed hypothesis, which excludes only the odd Weil representation when n = 1, does not suffice for the proof when n ≥ 2.)
items.locator: Appendix A.1, Proposition A.2 and its proof, pp. 1001–1005 (arXiv v3 pp. 29–32)
items.note: Proof, following Sakellaridis–Venkatesh §16.4: Poincaré series P_f on Mp_2n(A) built from a matrix coefficient of π_{v_0}, wave packets of principal-series Bernstein components at an auxiliary set S_0, and K_v-invariant functions elsewhere, lie in the ψ-generic cuspidal spectrum and realize ⟨R_y f_S, f_S⟩, so π_S is weakly contained in ⊕_i Π_i; exponent bounds and isolation in the Fell topology then force π_S = Π_{i,S}. The isolation step invokes an unproved Mp_2n analogue of Ichino–Lapid–Mao's Lemma A.2 (sourceIssues E3). Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18): statement corrected against the paper: The item copies the printed hypothesis, but the proof does not establish the proposition under it. For n ≥ 2, a ψ_{v0}-generic supercuspidal π_{v0} whose L-parameter contains S_2 has a non-supercuspidal θ_{ψ_{v0}}(π_{v0}). For such π_{v0} the step 'as shown in the proof of Proposition A.1, Θ^aut_ψ(Π_i) is cuspidal' (p. 1005) fails (new issue below). The note's account of E3 is also wrong: Ichino–Lapid–Mao themselves state the Mp analogue of their Lemma A.2 (E3 rejected). Minor points: ψ is a fixed nontrivial character of F\A defining the generic character (Gan–Gross–Prasad, §12), and 'principal series' means irreducible principal series (p. 1005, 'as in Remark 5.3'). Review note: missing; no stage plans it; route 1 is right. Every use in the paper (Proposition A.1, with π_{v0} the descent of a supercuspidal τ_{v0}) satisfies the corrected hypothesis. The Poincaré-series and weak-containment inputs of the proof have no item (see coverage).

items.name: Generic characters and uniqueness of Whittaker models for Mp_2n
items.statement: Let F be a number field, N the standard maximal unipotent subgroup of Sp_2n, and N(A) ⊂ Mp_2n(A) through the canonical splitting. A nontrivial character ψ of F\A defines a generic character of N(F)\N(A), again written ψ (Gan–Gross–Prasad, Astérisque 346, §12). For an automorphic form ϕ on Mp_2n(A), put W_ϕ(g) = ∫_{N(F)\N(A)} ϕ(xg) \overline{ψ(x)} dx. Let L²_{cusp,ψ-gen}(Mp_2n) be the orthogonal complement in L²_cusp(Mp_2n) (the closure of the genuine cusp forms) of the closure of the space of genuine cusp forms ϕ with W_ϕ = 0. By uniqueness of local Whittaker functionals for genuine representations of Mp_2n(F_v) at every place, L²_{cusp,ψ-gen}(Mp_2n) is multiplicity-free.
items.locator: Appendix A.1, proof of Proposition A.2, pp. 1001–1003 (arXiv v3 pp. 29–30)
items.note: MP.5 plans Fourier–Whittaker expansions on the cover; uniqueness of local Whittaker models for Mp_2n is not planned. Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18): statement corrected against the paper: Complex conjugate dropped. The page image of p. 1003 shows W_ϕ(g) = ∫_{N(F)\N(A)} ϕ(xg) \overline{ψ(x)} dx, and likewise (P_v f̃)(g) = ∫_{N_v} f̃(xg) \overline{ψ_v(x)} dx. With the bar, W_ϕ(xg) = ψ(x)W_ϕ(g) and P_v f̃ ∈ C_c^∞(N_v\G_v, ψ_v); the item's formula gives the ψ^{-1}-coefficient. Review note: missing; route 1 is right. For multiplicity-freeness the item needs uniqueness of Whittaker models for genuine representations of Mp_2n(F_v) (for p-adic F_v, Szpruch, Pacific J. Math. 232 (2007)), which no stage plans. MP.5 plans only Fourier–Whittaker expansions on the cover.

items.name: Exponent bounds and isolation for generic representations of Mp_2n
items.statement: (a) Let c_n = 1/2 − 1/(4n² + 1). Let Π be an irreducible genuine globally ψ-generic cuspidal automorphic representation of Mp_2n(A) whose global theta lift to the split SO_2n+1(A) is cuspidal. Then Π_v ∈ Irr_{unit,ψ_v-gen,≤c_n} Mp_2n(F_v) for every nonarchimedean place v (Ichino–Lapid–Mao, Duke Math. J. 166 (2017), Prop. A.7, deduced from their Prop. A.5, the Jiang–Soudry description of the Cogdell–Kim–Piatetski-Shapiro–Shahidi lift and the Luo–Rudnick–Sarnak bounds; ILM normalize the lift as the theta ψ^{-1}-lift of ψ_Ñ-generic forms). Here Irr_{unit,ψ-gen,≤c} Mp_2n(F_v) is the set of irreducible unitary genuine ψ-generic π whose Langlands data (Ban–Jantzen) are d(π) = [(L, δ)], with δ square-integrable on a Levi subgroup L of corank k and exponent P(π) in the image of [−c, c]^k in a*_L/W_L. For a finite set S, Irr_{unit,ψ_S-gen,≤c} G_S is the product over v ∈ S. (b) (The Mp analogue of ILM Lemma A.2, stated in ILM, App. A.) For c < 1/2 and every class [(L, δ)] with δ ψ-generic, the set Irr_{temp,reg,[(L,δ)]} Mp_2n(F_v) is open in Irr_{unit,ψ_v-gen,≤c} Mp_2n(F_v) in the Fell topology. In particular (L = G), every irreducible genuine ψ_v-generic square-integrable representation is an isolated point of that set. Hence every ψ_S-generic square-integrable π_S is isolated in Irr_{unit,ψ_S-gen,≤c} G_S.
items.locator: Appendix A.1, proof of Proposition A.2, p. 1005 (arXiv v3 p. 32)
items.note: (b) is asserted for Mp_2n without proof (sourceIssues E3). Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18): statement corrected against the paper: (a) loses the uniformity the argument needs. Ichino–Lapid–Mao, Prop. A.7 (arXiv:1404.2909v2, p. 27, read) gives one constant c = 1/2 − 1/(4n² + 1) for every place and every such Π, so the whole family {Π_{i,S}} lies in one Irr_{unit,ψ_S-gen,≤c} G_S. The item's 'for some 0 ≤ c < 1/2' reads as depending on Π. (b): ILM state the Mp analogue themselves (p. 27: 'In particular, the analogue of Lemma A.2 holds for G̃', with half-integrality from Gan–Savin and the SO(2n+1) case). ILM Lemma A.2 says that Irr_{temp,reg,[(L,δ)]} is open in Irr_{unit,gen,≤c}; isolation of a square-integrable π is its case L = G. The set Irr_{≤c} is used but not defined. The note '(b) is asserted without proof' is wrong (E3 rejected). Review note: missing; no stage plans Fell-topology isolation or Ramanujan-type exponent bounds for Mp_2n; route 1 is right. The Duke version could not be accessed (subscription), and GI cite its p. 1328. The numbers Lemma A.2, Prop. A.7 and Cor. A.8 match arXiv v2.

items.name: Proposition A.3 (globalizing discrete series of GL_2 with L(1/2) ≠ 0)
items.statement: Let F be totally real, S a finite set of places containing the archimedean places and v_0 ∉ S nonarchimedean. For each v ∈ S let τ_v be an irreducible square-integrable representation of GL_2(F_v) with trivial central character. Then there is an irreducible cuspidal automorphic representation T of GL_2(A) with trivial central character such that T_v = τ_v for all v ∈ S; T_v is a principal series representation for all v ∉ S ∪ {v_0}; and L(1/2, T) ≠ 0.
items.locator: Appendix A.2, Proposition A.3 (p. 1005); its proof, through the set-up on p. 1006 and the deduction from Proposition A.4 and Waldspurger's torus-period theorem on p. 1007, pp. 1005–1007 (arXiv v3 pp. 32–33)
items.note: Could be deduced from Waldspurger's nonvanishing theorem (Forum Math. 3, Th. 4) or Friedberg–Hoffstein; the paper instead uses torus periods, so that its main result is independent of that theorem. Proof: with S = S_∞ ∪ S_1 ∪ S_2 (S_2 the supercuspidal places), take D ramified exactly at S_0 = S_∞ ∪ S_1 (∪ {v_0} for parity), π_v the Jacquet–Langlands transfers and E/F totally imaginary quadratic with prescribed local behaviour, embedded in D; apply Proposition A.4 and Waldspurger's period theorem to get L(1/2, T) L(1/2, T × χ_E) ≠ 0. Review note: missing; no stage plans it; route 1 is right. The statement matches p. 1005. The deduction also uses the existence of D ramified exactly at S_0, of E with the prescribed local behaviour, and of the embedding E ↪ D (no item; see coverage), and local–global compatibility of Jacquet–Langlands at the ramified places (see jacquet-langlands).

items.name: Proposition A.4 (globalizing distinguished representations)
items.statement: Let F be a totally real number field, S a finite set of places containing S_∞, and v_0 ∉ S a nonarchimedean place. For v ∈ S let τ_v be an irreducible square-integrable representation of GL_2(F_v) with trivial central character. Write S = S_∞ ⊔ S_1 ⊔ S_2, where S_1 (resp. S_2) is the set of nonarchimedean v ∈ S with τ_v not supercuspidal (resp. supercuspidal). Put S_0 = S_∞ ∪ S_1 if #(S_∞ ∪ S_1) is even, and S_0 = S_∞ ∪ S_1 ∪ {v_0} otherwise. Let D be the quaternion division algebra over F ramified exactly at S_0, and π_v (v ∈ S) the Jacquet–Langlands transfer of τ_v to D_v^×/F_v^×; for v ∈ S_1, π_v = χ_v ∘ ν_v with χ_v quadratic. Let E be a totally imaginary quadratic extension of F such that: E_v is the unramified quadratic extension if v ∈ S_1 and χ_v is unramified; E_v is the quadratic extension attached to χ_v if v ∈ S_1 and χ_v is ramified; E_v ≅ F_v × F_v for v ∈ S_2; and E_{v_0} is a field. Fix E ↪ D and put G = D^×/F^×, H = E^×/F^×. Then there is an irreducible automorphic representation Π of G(A) such that: Π_v ≅ π_v for all v ∈ S; Π_v is unramified, and an irreducible principal series representation, for all v ∉ S ∪ {v_0}; Π is not 1-dimensional; and ∫_{H(F)\H(A)} ϕ(h) dh ≠ 0 for some ϕ ∈ Π.
items.locator: Appendix A.2, Proposition A.4 and its proof, pp. 1006–1008 (arXiv v3 pp. 33–35)
items.note: Follows Prasad–Schulze-Pillot, J. reine angew. Math. 616, Th. 4.1, with a relative Poincaré series P_f on H(F)\G(A). The paper uses their Lemma 4.4 at v ∈ S_∞, 'which continues to hold for v ∈ S_∞'; there G_v is compact, so an H_v-fixed vector gives the required matrix coefficient directly. 'Principal series' at v ∉ S ∪ {v_0}: Π_v is unramified, and generic because the Jacquet–Langlands transfer of Π is cuspidal. Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18): statement corrected against the paper: Not self-contained. 'As in Appendix A.2' hides the data that the statement depends on (S_0, D, the π_v, E ⊂ D). Also, the proof gives Π_v unramified for v ∉ S ∪ {v_0}. 'Principal series' follows because Π is not 1-dimensional, so its Jacquet–Langlands transfer is cuspidal and Π_v (D split there) is generic. The note says this, but the statement should carry both. Review note: missing; no stage plans it; route 1 is right. The proof (checked) uses (A.1), PSP Lemma 4.4 at v ∈ S, discreteness of H(F)\G(F) in H(A)\G(A), and a mean-zero f_{v_0} supported in H_{v_0}·∩_μ ker μ (finitely many quadratic characters μ, so the intersection is open) to kill automorphic characters. All these steps hold.

items.name: Matrix coefficients with nonzero relative projection (Prasad–Schulze-Pillot)
items.statement: Let G be a reductive group over a nonarchimedean local field, or a finite central cover of one such as Mp_2n(F_v), or a compact group. Let H be a closed subgroup containing the identity component Z of the centre, χ a character of H, and π an irreducible supercuspidal representation of G (any irreducible representation if G is compact) with Hom_H(π, χ) ≠ 0. Then there is a matrix coefficient f̃ of π such that g ↦ ∫_{Z\H} f̃(hg) χ(h)^{-1} dh is a nonzero element of C_c^∞(H\G, χ); translating f̃ makes its value at g = 1 nonzero (Prasad–Schulze-Pillot, J. reine angew. Math. 616 (2008), Lemma 4.4; for compact G, Schur orthogonality). Proposition A.2 applies it with H = N_{v_0}, χ = ψ_{v_0}, π = π_{v_0}. Proposition A.4 applies it with H = H_v, χ = 1, at v ∈ S.
items.locator: Appendix A.1 and A.2, proofs of Propositions A.2 and A.4, pp. 1004–1007 (arXiv v3 pp. 31–34)
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18): statement corrected against the paper: Missing hypotheses and an inexact conclusion. Prasad–Schulze-Pillot, Lemma 4.4 (J. reine angew. Math. 616, p. 14; arXiv math/0606515, read) is stated for a nonarchimedean field, a closed subgroup H containing the identity component Z of the centre, a character χ of H, and a supercuspidal π; the integral converges only because matrix coefficients are compactly supported mod Z. Given ℓ ∈ Hom_H(π, χ) and v with ℓ(v) ≠ 0, it says that for every nonzero v′ the function g ↦ ∫_{Z\H} v′(hgv) χ(h)^{-1} dh is a nonzero element of C_c^∞(H\G, χ); translating makes its value at 1 nonzero. In A.2 it is applied to the cover Mp_2n (H = N_{v0}, χ = ψ_{v0}, π_{v0} supercuspidal). In A.4 it is applied at S_2 (supercuspidal π_v) and at S_1 ∪ S_∞, where G_v is compact ('continues to hold for v ∈ S_∞'; Schur orthogonality). At v ∈ S_0 in A.2 the f̃_v are wave packets, not supercuspidal matrix coefficients. There, the nonvanishing of P_v f̃_v comes instead from the ψ_v-genericity of the irreducible principal series in the Bernstein component, as in Ichino–Lapid–Mao §4. Review note: missing; route 1 is right.

items.name: Local toric distinction (A.1)
items.statement: In the setting of Appendix A.2 (D ramified exactly at S_0, E/F with the prescribed local behaviour, π_v the Jacquet–Langlands transfer of τ_v), for every v ∈ S the representation π_v of G_v = D_v^×/F_v^× is H_v-distinguished: Hom_{H_v}(π_v, C) ≠ 0 (A.1).
items.note: Asserted without argument; it is the Saito–Tunnell criterion, planned in GZ.4. The cases were checked: at real places an odd-dimensional representation of H^×/R^× ≅ SO(3) has a vector of weight 0 for SO(2) ≅ C^×/R^×; at v ∈ S_1, χ_v ∘ ν_v is trivial on E_v^× because χ_v is trivial or χ_{E_v} by the choice of E_v; at v ∈ S_2, E_v is split and every infinite-dimensional irreducible representation of PGL_2(F_v) is distinguished by the split torus. Review note: planned: GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.4 is confirmed. It plans the toric Hom spaces and Saito–Tunnell for split and nonsplit tori, including archimedean discrete series, which contains (A.1). I checked the note's three case checks and they are correct: the odd-dimensional representations of SO(3) have an SO(2)-weight-0 vector; χ_v ∘ N_{E_v/F_v} = 1 because χ_v ∈ {1, χ_{E_v}}; and every generic representation of PGL_2 is distinguished by the split torus.

items.name: Waldspurger's theorem on toric periods
items.statement: Let Π be an irreducible automorphic representation of G(A) = (D^×/F^×)(A), not 1-dimensional, that is globally H-distinguished for H = E^×/F^×, and T its Jacquet–Langlands transfer to GL_2(A). Then L(1/2, T) · L(1/2, T × χ_E) ≠ 0, where χ_E is the quadratic character of A^× attached to E/F (Waldspurger, Compos. Math. 54 (1985), Th. 2; Jacquet, Ann. Sci. ÉNS 19 (1986)).
items.note: GZ.5 plans the Waldspurger period formula and the nonvanishing of toric periods 'exactly under the matching local distinction conditions and nonzero central L-value'. Review note: planned: GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.5 is confirmed. It plans the Waldspurger period formula and 'nonvanishing of a suitable toric period exactly under the matching local distinction conditions and nonzero central L-value', which contains the direction used here (period ≠ 0 ⇒ L(1/2, T)L(1/2, T × χ_E) ≠ 0). L(1/2, T × χ_E) is finite (T × χ_E is cuspidal), so L(1/2, T) ≠ 0 follows. Citations [89, Th. 2] and [38] (Jacquet; [37] in arXiv v3) are correct entries on p. 1011 and pp. 1015–1016.

items.name: The Jacquet–Langlands correspondence
items.statement: Local: let F_v be a local field and D_v the quaternion division algebra over F_v. There is a bijection τ_v ↦ π_v (Jacquet–Langlands) from irreducible square-integrable representations of GL_2(F_v) with trivial central character onto irreducible representations of D_v^×/F_v^×, characterized by the character relation on regular elliptic elements. Explicitly: for F_v = R, the discrete series of weight k (k ≥ 2 even) goes to the (k − 1)-dimensional (odd-dimensional) representation of H^×/R^× ≅ SO(3); for nonarchimedean F_v, the twisted Steinberg St ⊗ χ_v (χ_v quadratic) goes to χ_v ∘ ν_v, with ν_v the reduced norm; and supercuspidal τ_v go to irreducible representations of dimension > 1. Global: let D be a quaternion algebra over a number field F and Π an irreducible automorphic representation of (D^×/F^×)(A) that is not 1-dimensional. Then there is a cuspidal automorphic representation T of GL_2(A) with trivial central character such that T_v ≅ Π_v where D_v is split and Π_v is the local Jacquet–Langlands transfer of T_v where D_v is ramified.
items.note: R17.1 plans the explicit quaternionic local transfer; R17.3 the global transfer and its converse. Review (REV-PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18): statement corrected against the paper: The global part omits local–global compatibility at the places where D is ramified. The deduction of Proposition A.3 (p. 1007) needs it to get T_v = τ_v for v ∈ S_∞ ∪ S_1. The clause 'π_v = τ_v where D is split' belongs to the global statement, not the local one. Review note: planned, with a caveat. GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer:R17.1 plans the explicit quaternionic local transfer, including 'one-dimensional quaternionic characters/Steinberg twists', but it imports local Jacquet–Langlands from ET.6, which is p-adic only. The archimedean clause is covered only implicitly by R17.3's 'definite and indefinite cases'. R17.3 plans the global transfer, its converse and the parity condition.

items.name: Functorial lift from SO_2n+1 to GL_2n of generic cusp forms
items.statement: An irreducible globally generic cuspidal automorphic representation Σ of the split SO_2n+1(A) has a functorial lift T to GL_2n(A) with L(s, T, ∧²) having a pole at s = 1, L(1/2, T) = L(1/2, Σ), and T_v the local lift of Σ_v at every v (a principal series representation where Σ_v is one).
items.locator: Proof of Proposition A.1, p. 1002 (arXiv v3 p. 30)
items.note: The paper says 'We now take T to be the functorial lift of Σ to GL_2n(A)' without a reference; the standard sources are Cogdell–Kim–Piatetski-Shapiro–Shahidi (Publ. Math. IHÉS 99 (2004)) and Arthur's classification. Routed to ML.5 as in PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-25 (item ckpss-descent). Review note: missing; route 4 (ML.5, 'register ... transfers with exact hypotheses') is acceptable and consistent with PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-25. When stating it: T is an isobaric sum T_1 ⊞ ⋯ ⊞ T_k of pairwise distinct unitary cuspidal T_i, each with L(s, T_i, ∧²) having a pole at s = 1 (Cogdell–Kim–Piatetski-Shapiro–Shahidi 2004 with Ginzburg–Rallis–Soudry). Local compatibility at the ramified places is Jiang–Soudry's (Ann. of Math. 157 (2003); Invent. Math. 2004). The paper's equality L(1/2, T) = L(1/2, Σ) is of complete L-functions and uses compatibility at every place.

items.name: The local descent to Mp_2n
items.statement: Let τ_v be an irreducible square-integrable representation of GL_2n(F_v) such that L(s, τ_v, ∧²) has a pole at s = 0. Its descent π_v to Mp_2n(F_v) relative to ψ_v (Ginzburg–Rallis–Soudry, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 12 (1999) and J. Inst. Math. Jussieu 1 (2002); Ichino–Lapid–Mao, Th. 3.1) is an irreducible genuine ψ_v-generic square-integrable representation, supercuspidal when τ_v is. If Π is a globally generic cuspidal representation of Mp_2n(A) with Π_v = π_v the descent of τ_v, and T is the functorial lift to GL_2n(A) of its theta lift Σ to SO_2n+1(A), then T_v = τ_v (Ichino–Lapid–Mao, Prop. 4.3).
items.locator: Proof of Proposition A.1, p. 1002 (arXiv v3 pp. 29–30)
items.note: Stated as used; the cited statements were not read. Supercuspidality of π_{v_0} is needed to apply Proposition A.2. Review note: missing; route 4 is acceptable. In ILM arXiv v2 (read), Th. 3.1 is the descent bijection D_ψ: Irr_msqr GL_2n → Irr_{sqr,ψ_Ñ-gen} Mp_n, with γ(s, D_{ψ^{-1}}(π) × τ, ψ) = γ(s, π × τ, ψ). The identity that gives T_v = τ_v is Prop. 4.6 (→Θ_ψ(σ) = D_{ψ^{-1}}(L(σ))); Prop. 4.3 there is 'tempered with a Bessel model ⇒ generic'. GI cite the Duke version, whose numbering could not be checked (subscription). ILM's ψ/ψ^{-1} conventions must be matched with GI's 'descent relative to ψ_v'. Proposition A.2, as corrected, also needs θ_{ψ_{v0}}(π_{v0}) supercuspidal for the descent; see jiang-soudry-supercuspidal.

items.name: The partial L-function of a representation in L²_φ′(SO_2r+1) (3.1)
items.statement: Let F be a number field, φ′ = ⊕_i φ_i ⊠ S_{d_i} an elliptic A-parameter for SO_2r+1 and σ an irreducible summand of L²_φ′(SO_2r+1). Let S be a finite set of places containing the archimedean places and every place where σ or some φ_i is ramified, or where the L-parameter of σ_v is not ϕ_{φ′_v}. Then ϕ_{φ′_v} = ⊕_i ⊕_{j=1}^{d_i} φ_{i,v}|·|^{(d_i+1)/2−j} for v ∉ S, and the partial L-function of σ relative to the standard representation of Sp_2r(C) is L^S(s, σ) = ∏_i ∏_{j=1}^{d_i} L^S(s + (d_i+1)/2 − j, φ_i).
items.locator: §3.2, proof of Proposition 3.1, (3.1), p. 977 (arXiv v3 p. 10)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18 (coverage of the paper): The factorization of L^S(s, σ) over an A-parameter is a numbered formula used in the proof of Proposition 3.1. Item prop-3-1 mentions it only in its note, and no item states it. It combines arthur-global-so (a) with the eigenvalues of S_d at diag(|w|^{1/2}, |w|^{−1/2}). Route: MetaplecticAutomorphicFormsPartIIShimuraWaldspurger.

items.name: Analytic properties of partial standard L-functions of unitary cuspidal representations of GL_m
items.statement: Let τ be an irreducible unitary cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_m(A) and S a finite set of places containing the archimedean places and those where τ ramifies. The Euler product L^S(s, τ) converges absolutely, and so is holomorphic and nonzero, for Re s > 1 (Jacquet–Shalika). It continues meromorphically to C (Godement–Jacquet; Hecke for m = 1) and is entire unless m = 1 and τ = |·|^{it}. In particular, for self-dual τ, L^S(s, τ) has a pole at s = 1 if and only if τ is the trivial representation of GL_1(A), in which case L^S(s, τ) = ζ^S(s), with a simple pole at s = 1 and no zero on Re s ≥ 1.
items.locator: §3.2, proof of Proposition 3.1, p. 977 (arXiv v3 p. 10)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18 (coverage of the paper): These are analytic inputs to Proposition 3.1 that no item states (selfdual-types and strong-multiplicity-one do not). The argument also needs absolute convergence for Re s > 1, so that the other factors of (3.1) are nonzero at s = t + 1/2. Separately, item partial-l-function (range 2) should say that L^S_ψ(s, π) converges absolutely, and so does not vanish, for Re s > n + 1, not only that it is holomorphic there (see the new issue).

items.name: Local components of symplectic and orthogonal cuspidal representations
items.statement: Let φ_i be an irreducible self-dual cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_{n_i}(A) and v a place of F. If φ_i is symplectic (L(s, φ_i, ∧²) has a pole at s = 1), the n_i-dimensional representation of L_{F_v} attached to φ_{i,v} by the local Langlands correspondence preserves a nondegenerate alternating form. If φ_i is orthogonal (L(s, φ_i, Sym²) has a pole at s = 1), it preserves a nondegenerate symmetric form (Arthur, The Endoscopic Classification of Representations, §1.4). Consequently, for an elliptic A-parameter φ = ⊕_i φ_i ⊠ S_{d_i} for Mp_2n, φ_v = ⊕_i φ_{i,v} ⊠ S_{d_i} is a local A-parameter L_{F_v} × SL_2(C) → Sp_2n(C), since S_d is symplectic for d even and orthogonal for d odd.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18 (coverage of the paper): That φ_v takes values in Sp_2n(C) requires the local components of a symplectic (resp. orthogonal) φ_i to be symplectic (resp. orthogonal). This is Arthur's local–global compatibility, not a formal consequence of the pole of L(s, φ_i, ∧²) or L(s, φ_i, Sym²). Every localization ϕ_{φ_v}, including those in Theorem 1.1, depends on it, and no item states it.

items.name: The spectral decomposition of L²(Mp_2n) and the Hecke eigenvalues of its continuous spectrum
items.statement: L²(Mp_2n) = L²_disc(Mp_2n) ⊕ L²_cont(Mp_2n), where L²_cont(Mp_2n) is the closed span of wave packets of genuine Eisenstein series induced from P̃(A) for proper parabolic subgroups P = MN of Sp_2n, M ≅ GL_{k_1} × ⋯ × GL_{k_m} × Sp_{2n_0}, with data ρ = (⊗_i τ̃_{i,ψ}) ⊗ π_0 in the genuine discrete spectrum of M̃(A) and λ ∈ i a*_M (Langlands; Mœglin–Waldspurger, whose treatment covers finite central covers). The τ_i lie in the discrete spectrum of GL_{k_i} (Mœglin–Waldspurger: Speh representations of cuspidal ρ_i ⊠ S_{b_i}). Hence, at almost all v, the unramified Hecke eigenvalue family of the continuous spectrum at (ρ, λ) corresponds to the ψ_v-relative parameter ⊕_i (τ_{i,v}|·|^{λ_i} ⊕ τ_{i,v}^∨|·|^{−λ_i}) ⊕ ϕ_{π_0,v}. Together with Theorem 1.1 for Mp_{2n_0} and strong multiplicity one, this gives Remark 1.2.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18 (coverage of the paper): Remark 1.2 is an item (rmk-1-2), but the continuous spectrum it refers to, and the Hecke eigenvalue families there, are defined by no item. AS.4 plans the spectral decomposition for linear groups only. MP.5 plans genuine Eisenstein spaces but not the decomposition of L², and MP.8 says linear-group results do not transfer to covers automatically. Route: MetaplecticAutomorphicFormsPartIIShimuraWaldspurger.

items.name: Arthur's sign character ε_φ′ for φ′ = φ ⊕ S_{2r−2n}
items.statement: Let F be a number field, φ = ⊕_{i=1}^m φ_i a generic elliptic A-parameter for Mp_2n (φ_i pairwise distinct irreducible symplectic cuspidal automorphic representations of GL_{n_i}(A)), r > 2n + 1 and φ′ = φ ⊕ S_{2r−2n}. Then S_φ′ = ⊕_i (Z/2Z)a_i ⊕ (Z/2Z)a′_0 and S̄_φ′ = S_φ′/⟨a_1 + ⋯ + a_m + a′_0⟩. Put L_φ = ∏_i Sp_{n_i}(C), Arthur's substitute for the Langlands group (Arthur, (1.4.4)), through which every localization φ_v factors. Let φ̃ = ⊕_i Std_i : L_φ → Sp_2n(C) and φ̃′ = φ̃ ⊕ S_{2r−2n} : L_φ × SL_2(C) → Sp_2r(C). Let κ : S_φ′ ↪ Sp_2r(C) be the embedding onto the centralizer of the image of φ̃′, so that Std ∘ (κ × φ̃′) = (⊕_i κ_i ⊠ Std_i) ⊕ (κ′_0 ⊠ S_{2r−2n}), where κ_i(a_j) = −1 if i = j and 1 otherwise, κ_i(a′_0) = 1, κ′_0(a_j) = 1 and κ′_0(a′_0) = −1. Decompose Ad ∘ (κ × φ̃′) = ⊕_j ε_j ⊠ ρ_j ⊠ S_{d_j} as a representation of S_φ′ × L_φ × SL_2(C), with characters ε_j of S_φ′ (each trivial on the image of −1, hence a character of S̄_φ′), irreducible representations ρ_j of L_φ and integers d_j ≥ 1. For symplectic ρ_j put ε(s, φ, ρ_j) = ∏_v ε(s, ρ_j ∘ φ_v, ψ_v); it is independent of ψ, and ε(1/2, φ, ρ_j) ∈ {±1}. Then ε_φ′ = ∏_j ε_j, the product over those j with ρ_j symplectic and ε(1/2, φ, ρ_j) = −1. This is Arthur's (1.5.6), which defines ε_φ′ in the same way for every elliptic A-parameter of SO_2r+1, with L_φ′ built from Sp_{n_i}(C) or SO_{n_i}(C) according to the type of φ_i.
items.locator: §4.4, proof of Lemma 4.3, pp. 982–983 (arXiv v3 p. 14); Arthur, The Endoscopic Classification of Representations, (1.4.4) and (1.5.6)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18 (coverage of the paper): Lemma 4.3 computes ε_φ′, and through ε_φ = ι*ε_φ′ this computation feeds Proposition 4.4 and Theorem 1.4. Item arthur-global-so only names ε_φ′ ('Arthur (1.5.6)'). No item states the definition the proof uses: Arthur's substitute L_φ for the Langlands group, the embedding κ, the adjoint decomposition and the root-number condition.

items.name: Weak lift of a genuine representation of Mp_2n(A) to GL_2n(A)
items.statement: Let F be a number field, ψ a nontrivial character of F\A and π = ⊗_v π_v an irreducible genuine representation of Mp_2n(A). An isobaric sum Π = ⊞_j Π_j of cuspidal automorphic representations Π_j of GL_{m_j}(A), with Σ_j m_j = 2n (item strong-multiplicity-one), is a weak lift of π if, for almost all places v, the L-parameter of Π_v equals the L-parameter of π_v relative to ψ_v (Remark 5.3) composed with Sp_2n(C) ⊂ GL_2n(C). By strong multiplicity one, a weak lift is unique when it exists. Two cases are used. (a) Let π be an irreducible summand of L²_disc(Mp_2n) with A-parameter φ = ⊕_i φ_i ⊠ S_{d_i} (Proposition 3.1). Then ⊞_i ⊞_{j=1}^{d_i} φ_i|det|^{(d_i+1)/2−j} is a weak lift of π; for generic φ it is ⊞_i φ_i (4.2). (b) Let π be a subrepresentation of Ind_{P̃(A)}^{Mp_2n(A)}((⊗_i τ̃_{i,ψ}) ⊗ π_0), with τ_i cuspidal on GL_{k_i}(A) and π_0 on Mp_2n0(A), and let τ_0 be a weak lift of π_0. Then (⊞_i (τ_i ⊞ τ_i^∨)) ⊞ τ_0 is a weak lift of π (4.1), since at almost all v the ψ_v-parameter of the unramified constituent of the local induced representation is computed by Remark 5.3.
items.locator: Proofs of Proposition 3.1 (p. 978) and Proposition 4.1, (4.1)–(4.2), pp. 979–980 (arXiv v3 pp. 11–12)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18 (coverage of the paper): The proof of Proposition 4.1 compares two weak lifts, (4.1) and (4.2), by strong multiplicity one. The paper never defines 'weak lift', and no item does either; prop-3-1 and prop-4-1 use the notion only in their notes. Route: MetaplecticAutomorphicFormsPartIIShimuraWaldspurger.

items.name: The Jacquet–Shalika bound for unitary cuspidal representations of GL_m
items.statement: Let F be a number field and Π a unitary cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_m(A). For every place v, the L-parameter of Π_v has the form ⊕_j ρ_j|·|^{t_j} with ρ_j irreducible tempered representations of L_{F_v} and t_j ∈ R, |t_j| < 1/2. At unramified v this is |α| ∈ (q_v^{−1/2}, q_v^{1/2}) for every Satake parameter α (Jacquet–Shalika, 'On Euler products … I', Amer. J. Math. 103 (1981), 499–558, Cor. 2.5). At the other places it follows from the same Rankin–Selberg argument, together with the unitarity of Π_v (whose exponents come in pairs ±t): the complete L(s, Π × Π^∨) is holomorphic for Re s > 1 and has a simple pole at s = 1, the partial Euler product is nonzero for Re s > 1, and local factors have no zeros. Consequently, every localization φ_v of a generic elliptic A-parameter φ = ⊕_i φ_i for Mp_2n is almost tempered.
items.locator: §5.1, p. 985 (arXiv v3 p. 16), used without citation; also implicit in the proof of Corollary 4.2, p. 980
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18 (coverage of the paper): This claim makes Lemmas 5.1 and 5.2, Proposition 5.4 and Proposition 6.1 apply at every place of a generic parameter, so Theorem 1.4 depends on it. It rests on the Jacquet–Shalika bound at every place, which the paper uses without citation. The local-parameters note mentions the bound but no item states it, and no stage plans it: atlas searches for Ramanujan or exponent bounds find no automorphic stage. Route: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors.

items.name: Number fields with prescribed completions
items.statement: Let E be a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero. (i) There is a totally imaginary number field F with two distinct places v0 ≠ v1 such that F_{v0} ≅ F_{v1} ≅ E. (ii) In particular there is a totally imaginary number field F with a place v0 such that F_{v0} ≅ E. For E = R, every real quadratic field has two real places, and Q has F_∞ = R.
items.locator: Used without statement in the proofs of Lemmas 6.8, 6.10, 6.11 and 6.12, pp. 996–1000 (arXiv v3 pp. 24–28), through Corollary 6.7
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18 (coverage of the paper): Corollary 6.7 takes the number field as given. Lemmas 6.8–6.12 need one to exist for every p-adic field, and the paper never says so. Proof: by Krasner's lemma, approximate p-adically a product of two coprime minimal polynomials of generators of E by an irreducible polynomial g over Q; K = Q[x]/(g) then has two places with completion E. Take F = K(√−m) with m > 0 and −m a square in Q_p. Then F is totally imaginary and the two places split in F. Mathlib has Krasner (Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Field/Krasner.lean), and weak approximation is GlobalNumberFields Layer 1; no stage plans the statement. Route: MetaplecticAutomorphicFormsPartIIShimuraWaldspurger.

items.name: Dependence of theta lifts on ψ only through its square class
items.statement: Let F be a local field of characteristic zero, ψ a nontrivial additive character and a ∈ F^×. The Weil representations ω_{ψ_{a²}} and ω_ψ of Mp_2n × O(V) are isomorphic, via the dilation by a in a Schrödinger model. Hence θ_{ψ_{a²}} = θ_ψ, ϑ_{ψ_{a²}} = ϑ_ψ, Π_{φ,ψ_{a²}}(Mp_2n) = Π_{φ,ψ}(Mp_2n) with the same labelling π_η, and Proposition 6.1 for ψ is the same statement as for ψ_{a²}. Globally, for a number field F, finitely many places v_1, …, v_k and nontrivial characters ψ_i of F_{v_i}, there is a nontrivial character Ψ of F\A with Ψ_{v_i} in the (F_{v_i}^×)²-orbit of ψ_i for each i (take Ψ_0(b·) with b ∈ F^× chosen by weak approximation, the squares being open).
items.locator: Proofs of Lemmas 6.8, 6.10, 6.11 and 6.12, pp. 996–1000 (arXiv v3 pp. 25–28)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18 (coverage of the paper): The identities ϑ_ψ(σ′) = ϑ_{Ψ_{v0}}(Σ′_{v0}) and Π_{v0} = π_η relative to ψ both rest on the theta correspondence and the labelling being unchanged when ψ is replaced by ψ_{a²}. They also need a global Ψ with prescribed square classes at finitely many places. Neither fact is an item. llc-mp cites Gan–Savin Th. 12.1 only for the labelling. The Weil-representation isomorphism belongs with the local theta facts of MP.3. Route: MetaplecticAutomorphicForms.

items.name: ε-dichotomy and coherence of the local Shimura spaces
items.statement: (Gan–Savin, Compos. Math. 148 (2012), ε-dichotomy.) Let F be local and π ∈ Irr Mp_2n. The sign ε(V) of the (2n + 1)-dimensional space V with θ_ψ(π) ∈ Irr SO(V) is determined by the central character of π (relative to ψ) and the root number ε(1/2, π, ψ), the root number of its L-parameter. Consequently, if F is a number field, Φ a generic elliptic A-parameter for Mp_2n, and Π an irreducible genuine automorphic representation of Mp_2n(A) with Π_v ∈ Π_{Φ_v,Ψ_v}(Mp_2n) for all v, then the spaces V_v attached to Π_v satisfy ∏_v ε(V_v) = ε(1/2, Φ). In particular, if L(1/2, Φ) ≠ 0 there is a global V with V ⊗ F_v ≅ V_v for all v (item quadratic-spaces-global).
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 6.8, pp. 996–997, and proof of Lemma 6.11, p. 999 (arXiv v3 pp. 25–27); Gan–Savin [24]
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18 (coverage of the paper): The existence of the global V needs the local spaces V_v attached to Π_v to be coherent. The inner product formula alone only says which V give nonzero lifts. Coherence comes from Gan–Savin's ε-dichotomy together with ε(1/2, Φ) = 1, which holds because L(1/2, Φ) ≠ 0. No item states it: local-shimura mentions preservation of ε-factors, and llc-so-inner states η(z_φ) = ε(V), but neither relates η_v(z_{Φ_v}) to root numbers. The exact normalization of the local sign should be taken from Gan–Savin; it was not read here. Route: MetaplecticAutomorphicFormsPartIIShimuraWaldspurger.

items.name: Unramified theta correspondence from Mp_2n to smaller odd orthogonal groups
items.statement: Let F be nonarchimedean of odd residual characteristic, ψ of order zero, and V split of dimension 2r + 1 with r < n. If π ∈ Irr Mp_2n is unramified and its theta lift θ_ψ(π) to SO(V) is nonzero, then θ_ψ(π) is unramified, and the L-parameter of π relative to ψ is ϕ_{θ_ψ(π)} ⊕ ⊕_{j=1}^{2n−2r} |·|^{n−r+1/2−j}. In particular, for r = n − 1 it contains |·|^{1/2} ⊕ |·|^{−1/2}.
items.locator: Proofs of Lemmas 6.8 and 6.10 (tower property), pp. 996–998 (arXiv v3 pp. 25–27); complements (3.2)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18 (coverage of the paper): The tower-property argument must exclude a nonzero lift of Π to SO_{2n−1}, which is below the equal-rank range. Item unramified-theta states the unramified correspondence only for r ≥ n. The lift from SO_{2n+1} to Mp_{2n−2} is already covered by (3.2) with n replaced by n − 1. Route: MetaplecticAutomorphicForms.

items.name: Whittaker Poincaré series on Mp_2n(A)
items.statement: Let F be a number field, ψ a nontrivial character of F\A, G(A) = Mp_2n(A), and C_c^∞(N_v\G_v, ψ_v), P_v as in the proof of Proposition A.2. Let f = ⊗_v f_v with f_v ∈ C_c^∞(N_v\G_v, ψ_v), subject to three conditions. First, f_v = P_v f̃_v with f̃_v = ε on ε·K_v (ε = ±1) and 0 elsewhere, for all v outside a finite set, where F_v has odd residual characteristic and ψ_v has order zero. Second, f_{v_0} = P_{v_0} f̃_{v_0} for a matrix coefficient f̃_{v_0} of an irreducible supercuspidal π_{v_0}. Third, f_v = P_v f̃_v at a finite set S_0 of nonarchimedean places, with f̃_v in the Hecke algebra of a Bernstein component consisting only of irreducible principal series; such components exist, e.g. the component of a sufficiently ramified regular principal series. Then P_f(g) = Σ_{γ ∈ N(F)\G(F)} f(γg) converges absolutely, and P_f is square-integrable and cuspidal. For every genuine cusp form ϕ, ⟨P_f, ϕ⟩ = ∫_{N(A)\G(A)} f(g) \overline{W_ϕ(g)} dg, so P_f ∈ L²_{cusp,ψ-gen}(Mp_2n). Every irreducible summand Π with nonzero projection of P_f satisfies: Π_{v_0} ≅ π_{v_0}; Π_v lies in the given Bernstein component for v ∈ S_0; and Π_v is unramified at the places of the first condition. If S is a finite set of nonarchimedean places, f_S ∈ C_c^∞(N_S\G_S, ψ_S), and Ω ⊂ G_S is compact, then f_v can be chosen at v ∈ S_∞ with small support so that a compact U ⊂ G(A) exists with U^{-1} = U, Ω ⊂ U, supp R_y f ⊂ N(A)·U for y ∈ Ω, N(A) ⊂ N(F)·U and G(F) ∩ U^4·N(A) = N(F). Then ⟨R_y P_f, P_f⟩ = ⟨R_y f, f⟩ for all y ∈ Ω.
items.locator: §A.1, proof of Proposition A.2, pp. 1003–1005 (arXiv v3 pp. 30–32); after Sakellaridis–Venkatesh, Astérisque 396, §16.4
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18 (coverage of the paper): The central construction of the proof of Proposition A.2 (convergence, square-integrability, cuspidality, the orthogonality that puts P_f in the ψ-generic spectrum, its spectral support, and the unfolding ⟨R_yP_f, P_f⟩ = ⟨R_y f_S, f_S⟩). The prop-a-2 note only paraphrases it, and the blueprint needs it stated. Route: MetaplecticAutomorphicFormsPartIIShimuraWaldspurger.

items.name: Whittaker Plancherel support and weak containment (Sakellaridis–Venkatesh)
items.statement: Let S be a finite set of nonarchimedean places and G_S = Mp_2n(F_S). (i) Every irreducible genuine ψ_S-generic square-integrable representation π_S of G_S lies in the support of the Plancherel measure of L²(N_S\G_S, ψ_S); indeed it occurs discretely (the easy direction of Ichino–Lapid–Mao, Prop. A.4, after Delorme). (ii) Let {Π_i} be irreducible unitary representations of G(A), regarded as representations of G_S. Suppose that for every compact Ω ⊂ G_S and every f_S ∈ C_c^∞(N_S\G_S, ψ_S) with ⟨f_S, f_S⟩ = 1 there are c_i ≥ 0 with Σ_i c_i = 1 and unit vectors ϕ_i ∈ Π_i with ⟨R_y f_S, f_S⟩ = Σ_i c_i ⟨R_y ϕ_i, ϕ_i⟩ for all y ∈ Ω. Then L²(N_S\G_S, ψ_S), and hence every π_S in the support of its Plancherel measure, is weakly contained in ⊕_i Π_i. (iii) If an irreducible unitary π_S is weakly contained in ⊕_i Π_i, then π_S lies in the Fell closure of {Π_{i,S}}. So if π_S is isolated in a set containing every Π_{i,S}, then π_S ≅ Π_{i,S} for some i.
items.locator: §A.1, proof of Proposition A.2, pp. 1003 and 1005 (arXiv v3 pp. 30–32); Sakellaridis–Venkatesh, Astérisque 396, §16.4 and (16.8); Ichino–Lapid–Mao, Duke Math. J. 166, Prop. A.4
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18 (coverage of the paper): The proof's reduction step ('Since π_S belongs to the support of the Plancherel measure for L²(N_S\G_S, ψ_S), it suffices to prove ...') and its final step (weak containment plus isolation forces π_S = Π_{i,S}) use three facts of harmonic analysis that no item states. Route: MetaplecticAutomorphicFormsPartIIShimuraWaldspurger.

items.name: Cuspidality criterion for global theta lifts (Kudla, Rallis)
items.statement: Local (Kudla, Invent. Math. 83 (1986)): let F_v be nonarchimedean and π an irreducible genuine supercuspidal representation of Mp_2n(F_v). In the Witt tower of split odd orthogonal spaces V_{2m+1}, the theta lift of π at its first occurrence is irreducible and supercuspidal, and at every later member it is nonzero and not supercuspidal. Hence, if θ_{ψ_v}(π) on the split SO_2n+1(F_v) is supercuspidal, then π has zero lift to SO_2m+1(F_v) for every m < n. Global (Rallis): let Π be an irreducible genuine cuspidal automorphic representation of Mp_2n(A) whose global theta lifts to the split SO_2m+1(A) vanish for all m < n. This holds in particular if, at one place v_0, the local lift of Π_{v_0} to the split SO_2n−1(F_{v_0}) vanishes. Then the global theta lift Θ^aut_ψ(Π) to the split SO_2n+1(A) is cuspidal (possibly zero).
items.locator: §A.1, proofs of Propositions A.1 (p. 1002) and A.2 (p. 1005) (arXiv v3 pp. 29, 32)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18 (coverage of the paper): Two ingredients have no item: Kudla's first-occurrence theorem and Rallis's tower property in general. Item tower-property covers only generic A-parameters. The corrected Proposition A.2 rests on these two ingredients. Route: MetaplecticAutomorphicFormsPartIIShimuraWaldspurger.

items.name: Quaternion algebras with prescribed ramification and embedded quadratic fields
items.statement: Let F be a number field. (i) For every finite set S_0 of real and nonarchimedean places of F with #S_0 even, there is a quaternion algebra D over F, unique up to isomorphism, ramified exactly at S_0; it is a division algebra if S_0 ≠ ∅. (ii) A quadratic field extension E/F embeds in D if and only if E ⊗_F F_v is a field for every v ∈ S_0. (iii) Given finitely many places v and quadratic étale algebras E_v/F_v, there is a quadratic extension E/F with E ⊗_F F_v ≅ E_v at those places; if F is totally real, E can moreover be taken totally imaginary.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18 (coverage of the paper): The deduction of Proposition A.3 uses three standard facts: the existence of D ramified exactly at S_0 (with #S_0 even), the existence of E with prescribed completions, and the local–global criterion for E ↪ D. No item states them. (i) and (ii) follow from the Brauer–Hasse–Noether sequence, which the Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory roadmap (Layer 10) plans; R17.3 records the parity condition. Route: MetaplecticAutomorphicFormsPartIIShimuraWaldspurger.

routes.title: Metaplectic groups, Weil representations and automorphic theta kernels, Part II: theta correspondences and the Shimura–Waldspurger correspondence for Mp_2n
routes.brief:
A Part II of Metaplectic groups, Weil representations and automorphic theta kernels (MetaplecticAutomorphicForms): the local and global theta correspondence for the dual pairs (Mp_2n, O(V)) with V odd-dimensional, and its application to the automorphic discrete spectrum of Mp_2n, following Gan–Ichino, Ann. of Math. 188 (2018). Final theorems, as the paper states them. Theorem 1.1: for a number field F and a nontrivial additive character ψ of F\A, L²_disc(Mp_2n) = ⊕_φ L²_{φ,ψ}(Mp_2n), the sum over elliptic A-parameters φ for Mp_2n, where L²_{φ,ψ}(Mp_2n) is a full near equivalence class of irreducible representations π in L²_disc(Mp_2n) such that the L-parameter of π_v (relative to ψ_v) is ϕ_{φ_v} for almost all places v. Theorem 1.4: for a generic elliptic A-parameter φ, L²_{φ,ψ}(Mp_2n) ≅ ⊕_{η ∈ Ŝ_{φ,A}} m_η π_η, with m_η = 1 if Δ*η = ε_φ and m_η = 0 otherwise, where ε_φ(a_i) = ε(1/2, φ_i). The paper assumes Arthur's multiplicity formula (6.1) for non-split SO_2n+1; Ishimoto (IMRN 2024) has proved it for generic parameters, and this extraction routes it to ML.4. State Theorem 1.4 with that input explicit. Corollary 1.6: the generic part ⊕_φ L²_{φ,ψ}(Mp_2n), over generic φ, is multiplicity-free. Proposition 6.1 (local): for F local of characteristic zero, φ almost tempered and φ′ = φ ⊕ S_{2r−2n} with r > 2n + 1, ϑ_ψ(σ_η′) = π_η with η = ι*η′. Proposition 5.4: the members σ_η′ of Π_φ′(SO_2r+1) are nonzero, irreducible and pairwise distinct. Cover, in this order: (1) local genuine representation theory of Mp_2n: parabolic induction through the preimages of parabolic subgroups, the character χ_ψ, Langlands quotients for the cover (Ban–Jantzen), unramified representations and their ψ-relative parameters (Remark 5.3), and local Whittaker models; (2) the local Shimura correspondence (Gan–Savin for p-adic fields, Adams–Barbasch for archimedean ones) and the local Langlands correspondence for Mp_2n relative to ψ, with good and almost tempered parameters and Lemma 5.2; (3) J.-S. Li's theory: rank, stable-range lifts and the bijection (2.2), global rank, and Theorem 2.1; (4) global theta lifts: abstract and automorphic lifts, Kudla–Rallis irreducibility, the tower property, the Rallis inner product formula (Kudla–Rallis, Gan–Qiu–Takeda, Yamana), multiplicity preservation (Gan) and Furusawa's nonvanishing theorem; (5) the genuine discrete spectrum and near equivalence classes: Proposition 3.1, Theorem 1.1, and Remarks 1.2, 1.3, 3.2 and 3.3; (6) generic parameters: component groups, Proposition 4.1, Corollary 4.2, Lemma 4.3 and Proposition 4.4; (7) the comparison of local theta lifts: Propositions 5.4 and 6.1 by induction (Lemmas 6.2–6.4) and a global argument (Lemmas 6.8–6.12); (8) globalizations: Propositions 6.5 and 6.6, Corollary 6.7 and Propositions A.1–A.4, following Sakellaridis–Venkatesh and Prasad–Schulze-Pillot; (9) Theorem 1.4 and Corollary 1.6. Layers 1–4 are general theta-correspondence theory; design them so that other users of theta lifts can import them without the rest. The review (REV-PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18) rejected the three proof obligations that E1–E3 recorded. Gan–Savin's proof of Lemma 7.4 already covers s > −1/2. Adams–Barbasch's Theorem 8.4 and Kudla's framework give the induction principle as the paper uses it. Ichino–Lapid–Mao state the Mp_2n analogue of their Lemma A.2 in their Appendix A. Their arguments are still to be formalized, as items rather than open gaps. Import from: Metaplectic groups, Weil representations and automorphic theta kernels (MetaplecticAutomorphicForms) MP.0–MP.6, for the covers, the Weil representations, local theta modules and theta kernels on the cover. This extraction routes Howe duality, the conservation relation, the induction principle, the MVW involution and the unramified correspondence to MP.3. Modularity, automorphy and Langlands endpoint extensions (ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions) ML.4, for Arthur's classification of SO_2r+1, local A-packets, the local Langlands correspondence for the groups SO(V), Ishimoto's multiplicity formula for non-split SO(V), and Lemmas 5.1 and 5.5; and ML.5, for the lift from SO_2n+1 to GL_2n and the local descent. Automorphic L-functions and local factors (AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors) AL.3–AL.4. Endoscopic transfer and unitary trace comparison (EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison) ET.6. Automorphic forms on reductive groups (AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups) AF.1–AF.3. Automorphic spectral theory and trace distributions (AutomorphicSpectralTheory) AS.4, whose adaptation to the cover must be proved. Smooth representations of local groups (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups) SR.2–SR.3. GL₂ Automorphic Representations And Transfer (GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer) R17.1 and R17.3. Gross–Zagier formulas and arithmetic heights (GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights) GZ.4–GZ.5, for toric distinction and Waldspurger's period theorem. Quadratic forms and cohomological invariants (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/QuadraticFormInvariants) 6C–6D. Global quadratic forms over number fields (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/GlobalQuadraticForms) Layers 1, 7 and 8.

Corrections from the review (REV-PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18), to respect when stating the layers:
- Proposition A.2 needs 'θ_{ψ_{v0}}(π_{v0}) is supercuspidal' (the L-parameter of π_{v0} contains no S_2) in place of 'not the odd Weil representation when n = 1'. Jiang–Soudry's Th. 2.2(2), which the proof cites, fails for n ≥ 2 (Bakić–Hanzer, Prop. 3.5(2)). Proposition A.1 applies A.2 only to descents of supercuspidals, which satisfy the stronger hypothesis, so nothing downstream changes.
- In the proof of Proposition 3.1, the pole of L^S(s, θ^abs_ψ(π)) at r − n + 1/2 needs L^S_ψ(r − n + 1/2, π) ≠ 0. Take it from absolute convergence of the Euler product for Re s > n + 1.
- The automorphic theta integral uses the complex conjugate of ϕ(g) (p. 975), and the Whittaker functional of §A.1 the conjugate of ψ(x) (p. 1003).
- Hypothesis (6.1) must include the near-equivalence decomposition for non-split SO(V), which Lemma 6.10 uses. Ishimoto's published result is confirmed for generic parameters only.
- Normalize the Hasse invariant so that ε(V) = 1 on split spaces; the planned localHasse gives (−1,−1)^{r(r−1)/2} there.
routes.reason: MetaplecticAutomorphicForms constructs the covers, the Weil representation, the local theta modules (MP.3) and theta kernels and genuine automorphic forms (MP.4–MP.5). It has no layer for the theta correspondence as a correspondence (the local Shimura correspondence, J.-S. Li's stable-range lifts, the Rallis inner product formula) or for the discrete spectrum of Mp_2n. The paper's theory is new layers in that roadmap's direction, and nothing else in the atlas plans it. The Arthur-type classification is imported from ML.4, not planned again.

Howe duality, the conservation relation, Kudla's induction principle, the MVW involution and the unramified theta correspondence are local facts about the dual pair (Mp_2n, O(V)), which MP.3 owns. MP.3 asks for Howe duality to be 'pinned to an actual theorem'; Gan–Takeda (2016) is that theorem. PAPER-CHENEVIER-TAIBI-20 routed the unramified correspondence to MP.3 already.

ML.4 owns the classification inputs for classical groups (packets, multiplicities, local–global compatibilities) and keeps conditional hypotheses visible 'until the exact missing result and applicable replacement are verified'. The paper's hypothesis (6.1), with Ishimoto's proof, is such a case. The Vogan-packet correspondence for the odd orthogonal inner forms, and the irreducibility Lemmas 5.1 and 5.5, are properties of those packets. PAPER-CHENEVIER-TAIBI-20 routed Mœglin–Renard's packet results to ML.4 in the same way.

The functorial lift of generic cusp forms from SO_2n+1 to GL_2n and the Ginzburg–Rallis–Soudry descent are known transfers with exact hypotheses, which ML.5 registers. PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-25 and PAPER-JIANG-ZHANG-20 routed the same lift and the global descent to ML.5.

The archimedean local Langlands correspondence for GL_n is Langlands' classification of representations of real reductive groups, which fits AF.1's real representation theory. This follows PAPER-CHENEVIER-TAIBI-20's route; ET.6 covers only p-adic fields.
Strong multiplicity one for isobaric representations follows from the Rankin–Selberg theory AL.3 plans (Jacquet–Shalika 1981). It is a general GL_n statement, used here only as an input.

review.reason: I read Gan–Savin (Compos. Math. 148 (2012), PDF from Cambridge Core). Prop. 7.3 (p. 1674) gives the J_r with GL(Y_{k−r}) acting by |det_{Y_{k−r}}|^{(k−r)/2}. The whole proof of Lemma 7.4 (p. 1675) reads: 'the center of GL(Y_{k−r}) acts by the character |det|^{−s+t_1} … whereas on S(Isom(Y′_r, X_r)) ⊗ Ω_{V_{n−k},W_{n−r}}, GL(Y_{k−r}) acts by |det|^{(k−r)/2} … Since −s + t_1 ⩽ 0 and k − r > 0, we deduce that the above Hom space must be 0.' Only the inequality −s + t_1 ≠ (k − r)/2 is used, and it holds as soon as s > −1/2. Gan–Ichino need exactly this range. After arranging π = Ind_P̃(τ̃_ψ ⊗ π_0) as a standard module, τ has blocks δ_i|det|^{s_i} with δ_i unitary square-integrable and 0 < s_i < 1/2. The embedding σ = Ind_Q(τ ⊗ σ_0) therefore puts Gan–Savin's s at −s_i ∈ (−1/2, 0), block by block, as in the proof of Gan–Savin Th. 8.1(iii). The remark 'which continues to hold for s > −1/2' is a correct and immediate observation, not a step without adequate proof. Even as a gap it would affect nothing: the paper proves the p-adic case of Lemma 5.2 by citing Atobe (Math. Ann. 371, Th. 3.13) and gives this argument only 'for the convenience of the reader'. The extraction's kind (gap) and affects (the proof) should therefore be withdrawn, along with the matching sentence in the lemma-5-2 note.
review.amendedCorrection: None needed. For the record, the extension follows verbatim from Gan–Savin's own proof. Lemma 7.4 is stated for s ≥ 0 and a unitary discrete series τ of GL(Y_k). It asserts Hom(J_r, τ|det|^{−s} ⊠ π_1) = 0 for r < k. The proof compares central characters of GL(Y_{k−r}): on |det|^{−s}R_Q(τ) the centre acts by |det|^{−s+t_1}, with t_1 ≤ 0; on J_r it acts by |det|^{(k−r)/2}. For s > −1/2 this gives −s + t_1 < 1/2 ≤ (k − r)/2, so the Hom space still vanishes.
