Math. 113, §8 (read in the authors' preprint, whose Theorem 8.4 is 'Induction Principle I') works with 'an orthogonal space of signature (p, q) and W a symplectic space of dimension 2n, with no further restrictions' and arbitrary Levi decompositions. For any σ ⊗ σ′ that is a quotient of the Levi Weil representation ω_M it gives a nonzero Õ(V) × Mp(W)-map ω → Ind(σξ) ⊗ Ind(σ′ξ′). This literally covers the real stable-range pair (Mp_2n(R), O(r + 1, r)); the extraction's 'for the real metaplectic group' reading (equal rank only) is wrong. (2) F = C: Adams–Barbasch, J. Funct. Anal. 132, Cor. 3.21 (complex dual pairs; Mp_2n(C) is split). (3) F p-adic: Kudla's paper (read at GDZ) treats every dual pair (O(V_m), Mp(W_n)) of type (O, Sp), with its Jacquet-module filtration (Th. 2.8) and the cuspidal-support theorem (Th. 2.5), but it does not state the 'nonzero map to Ind ⊗ Ind' form. Adams–Barbasch say their proof 'is essentially the same as the proofs of ([Kudla], Theorem 2.5) and ([AB complex], Corollary 3.21)', and it carries over verbatim: a Levi-equivariant surjection ω ↠ ω_M ν from a mixed model (their Lemmas 8.5–8.6), a nonzero GL_k × GL_k-map S(M_k) → τ ⊗ τ^∨ (a Godement–Jacquet zeta integral), the quotient π_{η_0} ⊗ σ̃_{η′_0} of the smaller Weil representation, and Frobenius reciprocity. review.reason: The quotation is exact. I read Ichino–Lapid–Mao (arXiv:1404.2909v2; the Duke version GI cite is behind a subscription). Their Appendix A states the analogue explicitly on p. 27: 'We now treat the metaplectic group G̃ = Mp_n ... The above analysis works with obvious modifications. (See [BJ13] for the Langlands quotient theorem in this context.) In particular, the analogue of Lemma A.2 holds for G̃. (The half-integrality of R(δ) for generic square-integrable representations follows from the results of [GS12] and the corresponding statement for SO(2n+1).)' ILM's Cor. A.8 for Mp_n uses it. So GI cite a stated result, and the extraction's 'invoked without an argument' does not hold. The argument transfers. The proof of ILM Lemma A.2 uses Tadić's results on characters and the topology of the unitary dual (valid for finite central covers), the Langlands classification (Ban–Jantzen for covers), and half-integrality of cuspidal exponents of generic discrete series; this last holds for Mp, since the reducibility points for ψ-generic cuspidal data lie in {0, 1/2, 1, 3/2} (Bakić–Hanzer, arXiv:1902.07357, Prop. 3.5). With λ_m ∈ [−c, c]^k and c < 1/2 this forces λ_m → 0. Isolation of a square-integrable π_S is the case L = G of Lemma A.2, and the product over v ∈ S is immediate. So the recorded kind ('gap'), affects ('the proof') and correction are not right: there is no gap here. The same sentence's other input, {Π_{i,S}} ⊂ Irr_{≤c} via the cuspidality of Θ^aut_ψ(Π_i), does fail in the generality printed; that is recorded as the new issue.

sourceIssues.correction: Add that L^S_ψ(r − n + 1/2, π) ≠ 0. One route is absolute convergence of the Euler product L^S_ψ(s, π) = ∏_{v∉S} L(s, ϕ_v) for Re s > c + 1, where |Re s_{i,v}| ≤ c bounds the Satake exponents of the unitary unramified π_v uniformly in v; the bound c = n gives the printed range r > 2n + 1. A bound that avoids spherical-function theory on the cover: θ_{ψ_v}(π_v) to SO_{2r_0+1}, with r_0 = 2n + 2, is unitary (Li, Invent. Math. 97) and unramified with exponents {s_{i,v}} ∪ {r_0 − n − 1/2, …}. The unitarity bound for spherical representations of split groups then gives |Re s_{i,v}| ≤ r_0 − 1/2, and it is enough to run the proof with r > 3n + 2, which is allowed because the proof only needs some large r. If [93, Th. 9.1] in fact states absolute convergence, the fix is only to say so.
sourceIssues.reason: In (3.3), the factor ζ^S(s + r − n + 1/2 − j) with j = 2r − 2n has a simple pole at s = r − n + 1/2. The other ζ^S factors are evaluated there at 2, 3, …, 2r − 2n, so they are finite and nonzero. So L^S(s, θ^abs_ψ(π)) has a pole at r − n + 1/2 exactly when L^S_ψ(r − n + 1/2, π) ≠ 0. Holomorphy of L^S_ψ on Re s > n + 1, which is all the text invokes, does not exclude a zero at r − n + 1/2 > n + 1. The pole is essential: it is what shows that φ′ contains S_{2t} with t ≥ r − n. The rest of the argument is complete (see the status_comment on prop-3-1 for the dimension count behind the 'largest t' step), and Proposition 3.1 and Theorem 1.1 stand once the nonvanishing is supplied. [93] (Yamana, Invent. Math. 196) could not be consulted; the paper cites it for holomorphy only.

sourceIssues.correction: In Proposition A.2, replace 'if n = 1, then π_{v0} is not the odd Weil representation relative to ψ_{v0}' by 'θ_{ψ_{v0}}(π_{v0}) is supercuspidal'. Equivalently, the L-parameter of π_{v0} relative to ψ_{v0} does not contain S_2; for n = 1 this is exactly the printed condition. With this hypothesis the proof works as written. π_{v0} has zero lift to SO_{2n−1}(F_{v0}) (Kudla), so each Θ^aut_ψ(Π_i) is cuspidal (Rallis's tower property) and nonzero (Furusawa), and ILM Prop. A.7 applies. In the proof of Proposition A.1, justify supercuspidality of θ_{ψ_{v0}}(π_{v0}) for the descent of a supercuspidal τ_{v0} by one of two arguments. Either its L-parameter is irreducible (ILM Th. 3.1), so Bakić–Hanzer Prop. 3.5(1) or Atobe–Gan Th. 4.1 with Kudla applies; or apply Jiang–Soudry Th. 2.2(1) to the generic supercuspidal σ with lift τ_{v0}. Proposition A.1 and everything downstream are unaffected, because A.1 applies A.2 only to such descents: Propositions 6.5 and 6.6, Corollary 6.7, Lemmas 6.8–6.12 and Theorems 1.1 and 1.4.
sourceIssues.reason: The step fails for n ≥ 2. Jiang–Soudry Th. 2.2(2) (Ann. of Math. 157 (2003), p. 767, read) asserts that for n ≥ 2 every ψ-generic supercuspidal π of Mp_2n has a supercuspidal lift to SO_{2n+1}. This is false. Take n ≥ 2 and σ′ a generic supercuspidal representation of SO_{2n−1}(F_{v0}). By JS Th. 2.2(1), one extension σ′^ε to O_{2n−1} first occurs at Mp_{2n−2}. By the conservation relation n(σ) + n(σ ⊗ det) = 2 dim V (Sun–Zhu, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 28 (2015); checked on O_1 and O_3), the other extension σ′^{−ε} first occurs at Mp_2n. By Kudla, π := θ(σ′^{−ε}) is irreducible and supercuspidal. π is ψ-generic. The open-orbit computation behind JS Cor. 2.2(3) has stabilizer inside SO_{2n−1}, so both extensions of a generic σ′ give Whittaker functionals. Equivalently, θ_ψ(π) is the generic square-integrable subrepresentation of ν^{1/2} ⋊ σ′ (Gan–Savin). That subrepresentation is not supercuspidal. This agrees with Bakić–Hanzer (arXiv:1902.07357, Prop. 3.5(2)): for ψ-generic cuspidal σ whose parameter contains 1 ⊗ S_2, Θ_ψ(σ) is square-integrable and embeds in ν^{1/2} ⋊ (a generic cuspidal representation of the smaller group). It also agrees with the Atobe–Gan first-occurrence theorem. JS's proof of (2) applies the tower principle, a statement about O_{2n−1}-representations, to an SO_{2n−1}-representation. The lifts to Mp_{2n−2} and Mp_2n come from different extensions σ′^{±}, which is exactly the mechanism of the n = 1 exception they note ('supercuspidal Weil representations of SL̃_2(k) do lift to SO_1(k)'). GI's hypothesis mirrors JS's (and ILM Cor. A.8's) exclusion of the odd Weil representation only. For such a π_{v0}, Proposition A.1's argument does not show that Θ^aut_ψ(Π_i) is cuspidal. It can fail: theta lifts to Mp_2n of globally generic cusp forms on SO_{2n−1} with local component σ′^{−ε} at v0 are globally ψ-generic and cuspidal, and have Π_{v0} ≅ π_{v0}, but their lift to SO_{2n+1} is not cuspidal. Their unramified components have exponent 1/2, so ILM Prop. A.7 does not apply and {Π_{i,S}} ⊄ Irr_{≤c}. The isolation argument then breaks. Proposition A.2 is therefore unproved as printed for n ≥ 2 (not shown false), and its application is sound. Existing corrections searched: no erratum found for GI, ILM (Duke 166) or JS (Annals 157). Haan (arXiv:2212.05234, Th. 3.3) restates JS Th. 2.2 with only the n = 1 exception. Bakić–Hanzer describe the phenomenon without mentioning JS or GI. So as far as found, this is new. (Coordinator: recorded as a gap in a stated result, not an error. The false step is the cited Jiang–Soudry Th. 2.2(2), and Proposition A.2 is unproved for such π_{v0}, not shown false.)
